It reports the thread's newest run, if still going, sent a message, and not repeating a message the thread already holds (§5, item 5), as ThreadHistory.runInProgress, and the view follows it as a live run (AgentRuntime.follow): the same fold, states, tile and registry entry, from the run's first stored event. It is not followed while a session holds the thread, nor once the view holds how it ended: a run stopped here goes on until the backend finishes it. 8. Runs outlive views. RunRegistry holds sessions by ThreadKey and captures terminal outcomes, "because a view unmounts. A run that fails after the user navigates away must still be recorded". Only the cancel button cancels; navigation only stops observing (docs/send-cancel-lifecycle.md). 9. Citations belong to the turn. - A turn is the user message plus every run it spans. - MessageState is keyed by user message id, and RunFold accumulates turnCitations across a turn's runs. A resumed run's figures therefore survive a later searches clear. - Citations show on the turn's last assistant text message. This is a backend and client data limitation (docs/plans/citations-ui/plan.md).
path: ADR-006: The Thread Timeline Model — Runs, RunFold, Bands and One Layout

items.title: 3. Rules for Changing the Timeline
items.text:
These follow from §2. They are what a reviewer should check.

  • No placement logic outside layOutTimeline. A filter, gate or re-keying added elsewhere recreates the four-places problem. Change the function and its matrix instead.
  • Every new ChatMessage variant must be classified. _standsInForItsRun is an exhaustive switch, so a new variant is a compile error until someone decides whether it can host a band.
  • Every change to how events become conversation goes through RunFold. A rule implemented on only one path breaks parity. The parity suites fail on it, and only for the cases they cover.
  • Ids that must agree come from one function. noResponseMessageId keys both a run's outcome tile and its unclaimed band. Drop-tile ids are derived from the run id and event index.
  • The model never substitutes a client clock. Undated rows take the run's last timed event (RunFold.undatedRowTime).
  • A view may watch a run but never ends it. Cancelling is the user's action alone.
path: ADR-006: The Thread Timeline Model — Runs, RunFold, Bands and One Layout

items.title: 4. Consequences
items.text:
Positive

  • The question "where does this run's work render" has one answer in one place, and a property test that fails when it is wrong.
  • A thread reads the same live and after reload. That is checked event by event, not hoped for.
  • Malformed events and failed fetches degrade one row, not the run or the thread.

Negative / cost

  • ThreadViewState's merge of restored and fetched runs is the densest logic in the room module. It is the main hazard for #601.
  • layOutTimeline is called from three sites in the room module (ui/message_timeline.dart, ui/room_screen.dart, unread_boundary.dart) and from the mockup harness's drifted copy of the room screen (lib/src/mockups/chat/chat_screen.dart). They must pass the same inputs, or the unread boundary and the rendered timeline disagree.
  • The vocabulary is precise and has changed several times (§7). Code and reviews must use the current terms.

Enforcement

Rule Pinned by The layout invariant, over the full case matrix test/modules/room/lay_out_timeline_matrix_test.dart ("no band renders nowhere", "every band renders on a tile of its own run", "no tile renders two bands", "every run that ended reaches a tile") Drop over misplace test/modules/room/lay_out_timeline_test.dart Live and reload agree on messages, states, outcomes and bands test/modules/room/replay_parity_test.dart Live and reload produce the same layout, after every event test/modules/room/live_reload_parity_test.dart History taken only once the turn's last run was read test/modules/room/thread_return_test.dart, thread_view_state_test.dart A followed run ends as the live run of the same events packages/soliplex_agent/test/orchestration/follow_run_test.dart A run still going is followed once, and not after a stop test/modules/room/thread_view_state_test.dart ("a run still going on the backend")
path: ADR-006: The Thread Timeline Model — Runs, RunFold, Bands and One Layout

items.title: 5. Known Limitations and Open Questions
items.text:
From #619's "Not in this PR" and #566's known issues:

  1. There is no single turn model for live and reload yet. Still open:
  2. placement around a resumed client-tool run;
  3. merging history with a live client-tool session;
  4. seeding the session cache from a late history.

Client-tool support is best effort and not used in production. 2. Remaining display gaps. - A row created before any timed event is undated live but dated on reload. 3. Unhosted combinations. A system-role reply cannot host a band. The GenUiMessage combination is "unsupported rather than intended". Changing either touches layOutTimeline, TrackerRegistry and the tile together. 4. Backend assumptions. - Drop-tile ids match across paths only because the backend stores one event per streamed event. That assumption is unpinned. - The backend keeps no run status, which is why the registry files failures as feedback. - A run the backend lost (it restarted mid-run) is never marked finished, and its stored stream sends keepalives forever. A followed run therefore ends as cut off after 10 minutes without an event (defaultHttpTimeout). A live run that resumes after a dropped connection reads the same stream and has no such bound. - An unfinished run that is not the thread's newest is taken to be lost: it is neither shown nor followed. 5. Following a client-tool turn. - A followed run that waits on a client tool has the follower run the tool and resume the turn, as live does. A run followed in two places at once would be resumed twice. - A run already resuming a turn when the thread loads (its message repeats one the thread holds) is not followed: that needs the turn resumed first, as live resumes it, which is the turn model of item 1. Nor is one that sends a held message again, which following would show twice. 6. Mutation-testing survivors. #566 listed survivors (the whitespace guard, the active-run guard, a dead known-run entry). It is not recorded whether later work closed them.
path: ADR-006: The Thread Timeline Model — Runs, RunFold, Bands and One Layout

items.title: 6. Alternatives Considered
items.text:
What was tried, and why it was replaced:

Approach Replaced by Why Placement decided in four places (display filter, synthesis gate, tracker re-keying, replay bucketing) layOutTimeline (#566) Nothing checked the shared property; bands rendered nowhere with a green suite A synthesis gate that appended a "no response" tile when it guessed a run had nothing to show Unconditional parking (7e84ce07) The gate guessed without seeing the timeline; parking lets the timeline decide TextMessage overloaded with terminalReason flags The sealed NoResponseTile (c6ed6d59) Mixed display state into a wire type and leaked it Per-tile try/catch around rendering Drop tiles at the data layer (0fabfb60, #223) It caught nothing that build() throws and "gave false confidence" Separate fold logic for live and replay, and replay inside SoliplexApi RunFold on both paths (#619) The copies drifted Bands subscribing themselves Routing only through TrackerRegistry (79febc27) Production never used the self-subscription; tests did Reload bands bucketed by replayToTrackers against the replayed messages Reload feeding a TrackerRegistry, the one live uses, from replay's fold A second copy of the speaking rule, the band endings and the activities, which drifted from live A run-keyed band held until the response ended Handing the band to the reply as soon as it speaks (#578) The band sat on the loading tile Restore from the registry and skip the fetch Restore, then always fetch, history authoritative per run (#578) The fetch was skipped for turns the backend had not stored yet A red ErrorMessage under a surviving reply The outcome beside the reply (eb839986) It looked like a fresh error on every reload
path: ADR-006: The Thread Timeline Model — Runs, RunFold, Bands and One Layout

items.title: 7. Glossary
items.text:
Term Meaning Run One AG-UI run, folded by RunFold. Turn A user message plus every run it spans; a client-tool resume adds runs. Parked outcome Conversation.runOutcomes[runId], a NoResponseTile; the only record of how a run ended. Band An ExecutionTracker: a response's work, rendered under a tile. Claimed / unclaimed band Keyed by the message that spoke for it, or by noResponseMessageId(runId) before one does. "Claim" means only a band being taken. Tile A RenderedTile (message, band, besideReply). Band-capable A tile that may host a band: an assistant text message, a NoResponseTile, or a loading tile, provided it is not besideReply. besideReply A failed run's outcome shown after its surviving reply; hosts no band. Drop tile DroppedEventMessage: a failure recorded at its position in the run. Dropped band A band layOutTimeline could place nowhere; a defect, logged once. setAside Runs history read while the view keeps its own copy.

Retired terms: "orphan" (now "superseded" or "standalone"), "synthesis" and the no-response synthesis gate, runErrorMessageId, seedHistorical, and no_response_synthesis.dart (now run_ending.dart).
path: ADR-006: The Thread Timeline Model — Runs, RunFold, Bands and One Layout

items.title: ADR-007: Thread Labels — One Curated Catalogue, Applied by Owners and the Assistant, With No Visibility Rules Yet
items.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Authors: William Karol Di Cioccio
  • Supersedes: —
  • Superseded by: —
path: ADR-007: Thread Labels — One Curated Catalogue, Applied by Owners and the Assistant, With No Visibility Rules Yet

items.title: 1. Context and Problem Statement
items.text:
A thread could be found only by name, and only inside the room that holds it. Three paired changes address that:

Phase Delivers Frontend Backend 1 A lobby Threads tab listing a user's threads across every room, most recently active first, paged by cursor #508 soliplex/soliplex#1261 2 Labels: a catalogue, attaching labels to threads, @label search #512 soliplex/soliplex#1267 3 Auto-labelling: the assistant attaches labels after a thread's first run — soliplex/soliplex#1465

Two of these choices bind people outside this repo:

  • The catalogue is a shared wire contract with the backend.
  • Phase 3 lets a model act on users' threads.

A third question came up during review. A label's name is text that other users can read, so the label catalogue could expose sensitive information. That is a security question, and the answer was to not restrict label visibility for now, and to keep the door open. This record states that decision, why it is safe today, and where a restriction would go if one is ever needed.
path: ADR-007: Thread Labels — One Curated Catalogue, Applied by Owners and the Assistant, With No Visibility Rules Yet

items.title: 2. Decision
items.text:
• There is one catalogue of labels per installation.
  • Only administrators create, rename, recolour and delete labels.
  • A thread's owner attaches labels to it, and so does the assistant, once, after the thread's first run.
  • The assistant chooses only from the catalogue, picks at most three, and is off unless the installation names an agent for it (label_agent_config_id).
  • Every user can read every label's name.
  • No per-user visibility rule exists, and no schema is added for one.
  • The label editor warns administrators, every time, not to use names that reveal sensitive information.
path: ADR-007: Thread Labels — One Curated Catalogue, Applied by Owners and the Assistant, With No Visibility Rules Yet

items.title: 3. The Decisions, by Axis
path: ADR-007: Thread Labels — One Curated Catalogue, Applied by Owners and the Assistant, With No Visibility Rules Yet

items.title: 3.1 One catalogue per installation, curated by administrators
items.text:
Labels exist to cut across rooms: the Threads tab filters a user's threads from every room at once. That only works with one shared vocabulary. Curation keeps the vocabulary small enough to filter by. It also keeps the exposure in §3.6 in a few hands: every name is chosen by someone accountable for it.

Names compare case-insensitively through a stored lower-cased key. The server uses str.lower, not str.casefold, because the clients fold with toLowerCase and the two disagree on characters such as ß. A name would look free in the autocomplete and then collide on save.
path: ADR-007: Thread Labels — One Curated Catalogue, Applied by Owners and the Assistant, With No Visibility Rules Yet

items.title: 3.2 Owners attach; usage counts are for administrators only
items.text:
Only a thread's owner can change its labels, just as only the owner can see the thread.

A label's usage count spans every user's threads. Shown beside a name, it would reveal how much of that work exists, which the caller cannot otherwise see. So the server sends it only to administrators.

For everyone else it omits the count rather than sending zero. Zero would read as "unused", and the client would then offer a delete that is in fact destructive.
path: ADR-007: Thread Labels — One Curated Catalogue, Applied by Owners and the Assistant, With No Visibility Rules Yet

items.title: 3.3 Admin standing comes from AdminStatus
items.text:
The lobby shows its labels tab only to administrators. It decides who that is from the server entry's AdminStatus, which asks /v1/user/authz. That endpoint runs the same check_admin_access the label routes enforce, so the tab appears exactly when its writes would succeed.

An unanswered check reads as "no". The server gates every write regardless: a wrong answer in the client costs a 403, never a write.
path: ADR-007: Thread Labels — One Curated Catalogue, Applied by Owners and the Assistant, With No Visibility Rules Yet

items.title: 3.4 Auto-labelling reuses title generation
items.text:
Phase 3 mirrors soliplex.titles (soliplex.labels):

  • A throwaway pydantic-ai agent runs after the stream's end sentinel. It therefore never delays the reply.
  • It runs side by side with title generation (asyncio.gather). Each helper logs and swallows its own failure, so neither can cancel the other.
  • It runs only after a thread's first run. Running it on every run would put back labels the owner has since removed.
  • It skips a thread the owner has already labelled. With an empty catalogue it skips without making an LLM call.
  • It adds to the labels the thread carries at write time and never replaces them, so a label the owner attached while the agent was choosing survives.
path: ADR-007: Thread Labels — One Curated Catalogue, Applied by Owners and the Assistant, With No Visibility Rules Yet

items.title: 3.5 The assistant chooses only from the catalogue
items.text:
The agent's output type is built per call with a Literal over the catalogue's names, capped at three. A name it invents fails validation and never reaches the database, so the catalogue grows only through an administrator.

The names are also listed in the agent's instructions. Measured against gpt-oss on clear-cut conversations, three runs each:

  • the schema alone picked the right label 6 times in 9;
  • the schema plus the listed names picked it 9 times in 9;
  • the listed names cost one weak false positive in 3 on an off-topic message.
path: ADR-007: Thread Labels — One Curated Catalogue, Applied by Owners and the Assistant, With No Visibility Rules Yet

items.title: 3.6 Label visibility: no rules today, and why that is safe
items.text:
What crosses between users. Thread content does not:

  • every thread listing, read and write is scoped to its owner;
  • a label attached to one user's thread is invisible to every other user.

What every user shares is the catalogue:

  • every label's name, which any user can read;
  • usage counts, which only administrators see (§3.2).

So the exposure is exactly the set of names that administrators chose to write.

Mitigations:

  • Only administrators can write a name (§3.1).
  • The label editor shows labelNameNotice (lib/src/modules/lobby/ui/labels_view.dart) in both create and edit modes. It says that every user on the server can read label names, that the assistant applies them automatically, and that names must not reveal sensitive information.

Why no schema now. No visibility model has been decided:

  • Restricted per label, per room, or per group?
  • Based on which user attribute?
  • With what fallback when an attribute is missing?

Columns added before those answers would be dead fields that guess at the model. They would then constrain the real design when it comes.
path: ADR-007: Thread Labels — One Curated Catalogue, Applied by Owners and the Assistant, With No Visibility Rules Yet

items.title: 4. Consequences
items.text:
• Backend team: the routes in §3.2 are a wire contract. usage_count must stay omitted, never zeroed, for non-administrators.
  • Deployers: auto-labelling is off by default. Turning it on means naming an agent in label_agent_config_id. It costs one model call per new thread, and none while the catalogue is empty.
  • Administrators: label names are, in effect, published to every user.
  • Contributors: a later per-user visibility rule changes the places listed in §5. Nothing else should read the catalogue for users or for the agent.

Enforcement:

  • Backend unit tests cover:
  • the first-run gate, the empty-catalogue skip, and the add-not-replace write;
  • the Literal rejecting an invented label;
  • counts omitted for non-administrators.
  • test/modules/lobby/ui/labels_view_test.dart checks the notice in both dialog modes.
  • Label names themselves are checked only by review: no rule judges what a name reveals.
path: ADR-007: Thread Labels — One Curated Catalogue, Applied by Owners and the Assistant, With No Visibility Rules Yet

items.title: 5. Known Limitations and Open Questions
items.text:
Retrofit path, should label visibility ever be restricted per user. The change stays contained because every user-facing read of the catalogue goes through a few places:

  1. Backend catalogue read. GET /v1/agui/labels (ThreadStorage.list_labels) gains a filter on the caller.
  2. Auto-labelling. labels.maybe_apply_labels reads the catalogue with list_labels() in one place. Applying the same filter there, for the thread's owner, keeps the assistant from attaching a label its owner could not see.
  3. Labels on a user's own threads (get_threads_labels). This needs a policy decision: does a label that was hidden later still show on threads that already carry it?
  4. Usage counts. These are already administrator-only, so nothing changes.
  5. The client. It holds no catalogue of its own beyond the server's response, and the @label autocomplete, the properties dialog and the labels tab all read that response. A filtered response therefore needs no client change.

The data the rule needs (an attribute on the label, plus the user attribute it is checked against) is one migration once the model is decided.

Not covered by any retrofit: a name that users have already seen cannot be unseen. The notice is the only control at the moment a name is written.

Other limitations:

  • False positives. One off-topic message in three got a weak label (§3.5). The owner can remove it, and it is not re-added (§3.4).
  • No record of who applied a label. Auto-applied labels look exactly like manual ones. Showing them as suggested would need the backend to record which labels the model applied. That is a column with no consumer yet.
  • Timing. A label applied after the room's post-run refetch shows up on the next listing. Thread titles have the same timing today.
  • An unfinished first run. A thread whose first run does not finish is never auto-labelled, because by its next finished run it has two runs. Closing this would need a flag on the thread recording that it was auto-labelled.
path: ADR-007: Thread Labels — One Curated Catalogue, Applied by Owners and the Assistant, With No Visibility Rules Yet

items.title: 6. Migration
items.text: There is nothing to migrate on the client. The backend schema arrives with phase 2's Alembic revision (soliplex/soliplex#1267). Phase 3 adds no schema and is off until label_agent_config_id is set.
path: ADR-007: Thread Labels — One Curated Catalogue, Applied by Owners and the Assistant, With No Visibility Rules Yet

items.title: 7. Alternatives Considered
items.text: Alternative Why rejected Add visibility columns now, unused Dead fields that guess at an undecided model and would constrain it later (§3.6). Let any user create labels The catalogue sprawls past usefulness as a filter. Every name is readable by everyone, so open creation also widens the exposure in §3.6. One catalogue per room No filtering across rooms, which is the purpose of phase 1. Store labels in thread_metadata update_thread_metadata deletes and re-inserts that row on every title update, so labels would be wiped without a trace. Let the assistant write free-form labels The catalogue would grow with no review, and every invented name would become readable by every user. Auto-label after every run Puts back labels the owner removed. Record which labels the assistant applied A column with no consumer yet. Add it together with a UI that uses it.
path: ADR-007: Thread Labels — One Curated Catalogue, Applied by Owners and the Assistant, With No Visibility Rules Yet

items.title: ADR candidates
items.text:
As of 2026-10-09, main @ 67b846e3. This document lists the surfaces, structures, seams and contracts in this repo that deserve an Architecture Decision Record. It builds on architecture-overview.md and is the second step of the "Project Management 101" plan.

How it was produced. Five read-only Sonnet agents worked in parallel: recorded-decision inventory, shell and library contract, auth and security, agent/client/wire contract, and git/PR history (1,648 commits, about 300 PRs and issues). The load-bearing claims were spot-checked against code before writing. Items marked (unverified) were reported but not confirmed.

items.title: How to read this
items.text:
Each candidate has a kind:

Kind Meaning Work needed Retro The decision is made and shipped; its reasoning lives only in code comments, commit bodies or one person's head. Write it down: context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Cheap. Open The code embodies a choice nobody has explicitly made, or there is a live tension (open issue, known gap, contradiction). A decision meeting first, then the ADR. Amend An existing ADR or doc covers part of it and is stale or too broad. Edit or split the existing record.

Priority.

  • P1: a wrong or unrecorded call here constrains forks, deployers, IdP operators or the backend team, or has security impact.
  • P2: a contributor convention that is costly to reverse.
  • P3: useful to pin down, but low reversal cost.

"Who is bound" names whoever has to know about the decision outside this repo's maintainers.

items.title: Housekeeping on existing records
items.text:
Done in #608, except splitting ADR-001, which was deferred: its axes are numbered, so it can be split when one of them changes.

Do these before writing new ADRs. They are small and they set the template.

  • ADR-003 is Proposed but shipped. Flavor and FlavorTheme are in lib/src/core/flavor.dart. Mark it Accepted. Its §2 blockquote about runSoliplexShell taking a builder was patched in place, so record it as an amendment instead.
  • ADR-001 bundles six decisions. These include the ThreadKey record, ownership-based discovery and runtime-owned disposal. The repo-wide rule "Riverpod is DI only, signals for state" sits in §5.3 as a rejected alternative. Lift that rule into its own record, or into C13.
  • docs/plans/0001-app-shell/proposal.md is stale. It says modules use "no base class or registry", but AppModule replaced ModuleContribution in da882974. Add a superseded note.
  • docs/developer-setup.md is stale. It still describes ag_ui as a git dependency with Git LFS. pubspec.lock shows the hosted pub.dev 0.3.0.
  • docs/adr/ has no index. Add a README.md with the template, the status vocabulary (Proposed, Accepted, Superseded, Deprecated) and a table of ADRs. AGENTS.md's "Key Documentation" lists neither ADRs nor diagnostics-known-risks.md.
  • Template. Keep the existing numbered shape:
  • header bullets: Status, Date, Authors, Supersedes, Superseded by, Amends;
  • §1 Context;
  • §2 Decision;
  • §3 Decisions by axis;
  • Consequences;
  • Alternatives (as a table).

Retro ADRs can drop Migration.

items.title: C01 Library public API and compatibility policy (Open, P1)
items.text:
• Today.
  • lib/soliplex_frontend.dart exports a curated surface: AppModule, ModuleRoutes, Flavor, ShellConfig, buildRouter, standard, standardFlavor, ServerManager, AuthState, and a show-listed subset of go_router, design and logging.
  • Two tests guard it: test/barrel_module_authoring_test.dart and test/barrel_reexport_test.dart.
  • All packages are publish_to: none. The app is 0.107.0+93, and soliplex_client is 1.0.0-dev.
  • soliplex_agent re-exports most of soliplex_client, and the client re-exports ag_ui (pre-1.0) wholesale. Forks therefore inherit a third-party wire type as public API.
  • Why. Forks build on this surface (CLAUDE.md: "runnable app and importable library"). There is no statement of what is stable, how breaking changes are versioned, or whether forks may import the packages directly. The CHANGELOG already carries "Library consumers (breaking)" bullets for agent types the barrel does not export.
  • Decide.
  • Is the barrel the only stable surface?
  • Is the library version separate from the app's build number?
  • Should the internal DI providers that leak out today (serverManagerProvider, inactivityLogoutFlagsProvider) be exported?
  • Should ag_ui sit behind an anti-corruption layer?
  • Which packages do forks consume?

items.title: C02 Module composition contract (Retro, P1)
items.text:
• Today.
  • ShellConfig.fromModules (lib/src/core/shell_config.dart) validates namespaces, routes and public paths. It builds modules in registration order and disposes them in reverse. On abort it tears down every module.
  • ShellConfig.redirect admits declared public paths first. Module redirects then run in order, and the first non-null result wins.
  • publicPaths must belong to the declaring module's own routes (router.dart, validateModulePublicPaths).
  • The embedder owns dispose.
  • Why. This is the extension contract for every fork module. Two things are security-relevant behaviour: the redirect order, which is implied by the order modules are registered, and the rule that public paths belong to their module. A hand-built router silently drops an in-flight sign-in (comment in auth_module.dart). Origin: da882974, ADR-003.

items.title: C03 Module layering and inter-module contracts (Open, P1)
items.text:
• Today.
  • core/ imports auth, lobby and room storage (removed_server_cleanup.dart, inactivity/*). lobby and room import each other.
  • lib/src/interfaces/ holds only the sealed AuthState. Everything else crosses modules by concrete import or constructor injection.
  • Why. CLAUDE.md says modules are "included/excluded by presence". Today a fork cannot drop lobby or room. Root cause: d6085bec moved cleanup into core.
  • Decide.
  • The layering rule.
  • Whether interfaces/ becomes the real contract layer.
  • How per-server cleanup is registered.
  • How the rule is enforced in CI.
  • Tracked in #607; related to #23 (split ServerManager).

items.title: C04 Server identity, alias and URL scheme (Open, P1)
items.text:
• Today.
  • serverIdFromUrl(url) => url.origin (lib/src/modules/auth/server_entry.dart:10) is the storage and session key.
  • aliasFromUrl replaces dots in the host with dashes, appends -port, and adds -2, -3 and so on when an alias collides. It is persisted and used in paths (/room/:serverAlias/:roomId/...).
  • Lobby uses ?server=<serverId>, so one server has two identifiers.
  • Why.
  • Web URLs and bookmarks are user-facing.
  • The alias is lossy: http and https on one host collide, and collision suffixes depend on the order servers were added. A shared link can therefore open a different server on another device.
  • Same-origin backends on different paths cannot coexist.
  • The direction toward shared databases builds on this model.
  • Decide.
  • A stable identifier in the path, versus the alias.
  • Whether one origin can hold several servers or accounts.
  • What happens to bookmarks when a server is renamed.

items.title: C18 Device-local persistence scheme (Retro, P2)
items.text:
• Today.
  • core/keyed_storage.dart builds percent-encoded composite keys with serverId first, and uses an unauthenticated bucket.
  • core/storage_migration.dart keeps a single monotonic schema version (1) and runs best-effort.
  • Tokens are in flutter_secure_storage; everything else is in SharedPreferences.
  • Read markers are swept by key prefix.
  • Why. The keys are on-disk user data, so changing them needs a migration. Every new store must follow the convention and register for cleanup on server removal. Today that registration is a hard-coded list in core (C03).

items.title: C19 Platform split conventions (Retro, P2)
items.text:
• Today. Three mechanisms coexist:
  • conditional imports, mostly on dart.library.js_interop, with a few on dart.library.io;
  • kIsWeb branches;
  • the injected PlatformConstraints.
  • Why. Contributors need a rule for which mechanism to use. Some failures only show at runtime on web: Isolate.run compiles but throws, and Platform.* throws.

items.title: C05 Web sign-in via backend BFF and token custody on web (Open, P1)
items.text:
• Today. Web signs in through the backend (/api/login/{provider}, a full-page redirect); native uses flutter_appauth. Sessions persist through SecureServerStorage on every platform.
  • Why. It binds the backend to the login contract, and the web and native flows rest on two different trust models.
  • Decide. The token-custody posture on web. Security specifics are tracked privately until fixed; ask the maintainers.

items.title: C06 Sign-out and IdP session end (Retro + Open, P1)
items.text:
• Today.
  • Signing out of or removing any server with a session triggers RP-initiated logout at the IdP (server_logout.dart; ed513e41, 50112f68).
  • Native. end_session runs first, and local state is cleared only if it succeeds. A user therefore cannot remove a server while the IdP is unreachable.
  • Web. Local state is cleared first, then the app navigates to the IdP, which may be abandoned.
  • Why. The asymmetry is deliberate but easy to re-litigate. The server_logout.dart docstring proposes a BFF logout endpoint, which would be a backend commitment.

items.title: C07 User identity and in-memory isolation (Open, P1)
items.text:
• Today. AuthSession.currentUserId derives the user from the access token; room/user_switch_teardown.dart evicts in-memory stores when it changes, and persisted state is partitioned by identity.
  • Why. The identity source is an assumption IdP operators are not told about, the partition scheme is baked into storage keys, and every new cache must opt in to eviction by hand.
  • Decide. The identity source, and an enforced registry of caches that must be evicted. Security specifics are tracked privately until fixed; ask the maintainers.

items.title: C08 Rendering untrusted model output (Open, P1)
items.text:
• Today. Model output renders as markdown with images, SVG code blocks, LaTeX and tappable links (room/ui/markdown/, shared/markdown/).
  • Why. Model output is attacker-influenced (prompt injection through documents), and forks inherit whatever policy the renderer has.
  • Decide. A rendering policy for images, links and embedded formats, and whether a flavor can tighten it. Security specifics are tracked privately until fixed; ask the maintainers.

items.title: C09 Logging privacy and diagnostics exposure (Amend + Open, P1)
items.text:
• Today. The CLAUDE.md rule "never log a user/backend-supplied value; use describeFailure" is enforced by review only. HttpRedactor redacts captured HTTP traffic by name. soliplex_logging's LogManager replaced dart:developer (9d66cea7, 660a29e6).
  • Why. A security boundary held up by convention; it binds every contributor and fork. docs/diagnostics-known-risks.md lists the open questions.
  • Decide. Redaction of log records, a lint or CI check, and the diagnostics screen's exposure. Promote the CLAUDE.md section and the risk register into one ADR.

items.title: C20 OIDC deployment requirements (Retro, P2)
items.text:
• Today.
  • Every discovery endpoint must share the discovery URL's origin (soliplex_client/lib/src/auth/oidc_discovery.dart), or sign-in fails.
  • Native needs a public client and the ai.soliplex.client://callback redirect.
  • Sign-out needs end_session_endpoint and post-logout redirect URIs.
  • Why. These are requirements for IdP operators (split-host Keycloak and custom domains fail) that are currently discoverable only by failing. Write an operator-facing section alongside the ADR.

items.title: C22 Inactivity logout policy (Open, P3)
items.text:
• Today.
  • A warning after 10 minutes idle, then a local logout after a 5-minute grace period (core/inactivity/).
  • Configurable per flavor at compile time; it can be disabled.
  • Decide.
  • Whether the logout should also end the IdP session.
  • Whether the policy should come from the backend.
  • Whether a sleeping tab counts as idle (#409).

items.title: C10 Backend compatibility contract (Open, P1)
items.text:
• Today.
  • ragStateKey = 'rag' and ragSourcesKey = 'sources' (soliplex_client/lib/src/application/rag_snapshot.dart) must match haiku.rag's STATE_NAMESPACE.
  • One schema snapshot (haiku-rag-0.89.0.json) and a drift test guard the mirror.
  • Support for haiku.rag 0.40 was dropped in favour of a single version (73d44744, #414).
  • Code that no supported backend reaches is pruned (fd4328b6, c9f8165e).
  • Capability is detected by skill, not by config flag (#452 and #455). Activities are rendered from the AG-UI envelope, not from backend schemas (b39e190a).
  • getBackendVersionInfo exists but gates no behaviour (not exhaustively checked).
  • Why. This is the tightest coupling to another team. A key rename silently breaks citations and filters. There is no stated window of supported backend versions and no feature-detection rule.
  • Decide.
  • The supported range: N backend versions, a minimum version, and how the app behaves outside it.
  • Detection by skill versus by version.
  • Who owns the snapshot refresh.
  • Whether the backend should publish a versioned state schema.

items.title: C11 Run lifecycle and failure reporting (Amend + Open, P1)
items.text:
• Today. docs/send-cancel-lifecycle.md states the rule: only the cancel button cancels, and navigation only stops observing. RunRegistry keeps runs alive across navigation. For a failed run that has a runId, run_registry.dart posts an automatic thumbsDown feedback. The comment explains that the backend keeps no queryable run status.
  • Why. The lifecycle doc is the strongest de-facto ADR in the repo. Auto-feedback uses the user-feedback table as a failure log, which skews feedback analytics and is a workaround for a missing backend API.
  • Decide. Whether to keep auto-feedback or ask the backend for a run-status or telemetry endpoint. Then promote the lifecycle doc to an ADR.

items.title: C12 Timeline, runs and bands model (Retro, P1)
items.text:
• Today.
  • layOutTimeline is a single pure function. Its invariant is that every ended run has a hosting tile and every band attaches exactly once.
  • The parked outcome is the only record of how a run ended.
  • Runs, bands and the registry form the central concept (#566, #578; cc1fb454, 7e84ce07).
  • Why. This is the most-churned area: room_screen.dart has 206 touches, thread_view_state.dart 73 and run_orchestrator.dart 63. It has been rewritten several times: NoResponseTile was added and later deleted, and the band vocabulary was renamed. Pin the reasoning before #601 splits _RoomScreenState.

items.title: C13 Signals convention and the 7.x migration (Open, P1)
items.text:
• Today.
  • CLAUDE.md mandates signal.watch(context) and Watch(...), and says Riverpod is DI only. A grep found no FutureProvider, AsyncNotifier or StateNotifier.
  • signals 7.x deprecates both mandated APIs. Adopting it fails the zero-warning gate (#314, about 30 sites).
  • Open issues #52 and #54 argue for replacing one-shot or error signals with returned values or FutureBuilder.
  • Why. The mandated convention is deprecated upstream, so a decision is forced.
  • Decide.
  • The new subscription idiom.
  • When to use a signal and when to use a Future.
  • Whether to amend ADR-001 or write a new ADR.

items.title: C14 HTTP client stack and token refresh (Retro, P2)
items.text:
• Today.
  • The chain, outermost first: Concurrency (max 6), Refreshing, Authenticated, Observable, Platform. Built by createAgentHttpClient.
  • Refresh uses a separate unauthenticated plainClient: the probe and refresh clients were split and then reverted to one (6078f08b).
  • invalid_grant puts the session in ExpiredSession, which a later refresh can revive. Network errors and unexpected errors do not expire the session.
  • Platform clients: cupertino_http on Apple, XHR on web, dart:io elsewhere.
  • Why. The order matters:
  • the redactor sees the injected headers;
  • retries re-run token injection;
  • the expire-or-retry choice decides whether a user gets locked out.

items.title: C15 Stream resume, history replay and failures-as-data (Retro, P2)
items.text:
• Today.
  • Resume. On a dropped stream, Last-Event-ID resume is tried up to 5 times with 500 ms to 8 s backoff and ±20% jitter (soliplex_client/lib/src/http/resume_policy.dart).
  • History. It is rebuilt by replaying stored run events through the same reducer as the live stream (SoliplexApi._replayEventsToHistory).
  • Bad events. An undecodable event becomes a DroppedEventMessage tile. A per-tile try/catch was tried and reverted (0fabfb60). Citations fail soft, raising ThreadStateWarnings.
  • Why. This assumes the backend keeps a resumable event log and per-run event retrieval. Keeping replay identical to live behaviour is subtle. "A failure is data, not an exception" is a principle worth stating once.

items.title: C16 Error taxonomy as a UI contract (Retro, P2)
items.text:
• Today.
  • The SoliplexException family is: Auth, PermissionDenied, Network, Api, NotFound, Cancelled, MalformedResponse, Unexpected.
  • HttpTransport maps 401 to Auth, 403 to PermissionDenied, 404 to NotFound, and everything else to Api.
  • 429 and 5xx have no dedicated types, but FailureReason has rateLimited (mapping not traced).
  • Why. The UI and forks branch on these types, so adding or splitting one is a breaking change (C01).

items.title: C17 Client-side tools, approval and host APIs (Open, P2)
items.text:
• Today.
  • A flavor supplies ToolRegistry per room. The standard flavor's is empty.
  • Approval is a SessionExtension and denies by default when none is registered.
  • HumanApprovalExtension auto-denies on cancel.
  • The host APIs (AgentApi, HostApi, BlackboardApi, FormApi) and the interpreter-shaped PlatformConstraints flags have no consumer in the standard flavor.
  • Why. This decides who may run code on a user's device on the model's say-so. If the host APIs are aspirational, they are public surface with no owner.
  • Decide.
  • The intent of this surface: keep, document, or delete.
  • Which tools must require approval.

items.title: C21 Multi-database thread semantics (Retro, P2)
items.text:
• Today.
  • A thread's database set is frozen by its first message, so that "evidence stays comparable" (#563).
  • The sources wire shape and MISSING marker follow backend issue #1322.
  • Why. It is a cross-repo contract and a product rule. Both are recorded only in commits and personal notes.

items.title: C23 Time handling (Retro, P3)
items.text: createdAt is nullable. No client clock is used on the display path, and UTC is stamped at the marker-store boundary (94061061, a7a05fa7, 3c46382c).

items.title: C24 Product constraints that bind engineering (Retro, P3)
items.text:
Some product calls currently live only in commit bodies:

  • "No new snackbars" (84b62fc4; the commit cites docs/plans/home-server-list/known-issues.md, which is not on main).
  • Classification markings are theme-only, with no wire field and no per-room value (#319–#322).

Record them in one place so they stop being rediscovered.

items.title: C25 Design package boundary and token governance (Amend ADR-002, P3)
items.text:
• soliplex_design was extracted as a package (b127f3bc, #274), and its boundary keeps renderer dependencies out of it.
  • Adding a token requires approval and changes to design_system/ in the same commit.
  • The CLAUDE.md hard rules are enforced only by a hygiene test and a review checklist.

items.title: C26 Boot validation and theme requirements (Amend ADR-003, P3)
items.text:
• ShellConfigurationError reaches the screen verbatim.
  • Any theme, including the full-token-control tier, must carry the SoliplexTheme extension or it is rejected at boot.

items.title: Suggested first batch
items.text:
Start with the items that are cheap or that block other work:

  1. Housekeeping (above). This is a single small PR.
  2. Decision meetings for the Open P1s that bind other parties:
  3. C05, C07 and C08 (security posture);
  4. C10 and C11 (with the backend team);
  5. C01 (with fork consumers);
  6. C13 (forced by #314).
  7. Retro ADRs that de-risk the next refactors:
  8. C02 and C03, before #607;
  9. C12, before #601.
  10. P2 retro ADRs. These can be written by one person per area from the evidence cited here.

items.title: Architecture mapping workflow
items.text: A reusable recipe for producing an architecture-and-boundaries overview of a repository with a multi-agent Claude Code workflow. It produced architecture-overview.md for this repo on 2026-10-09, the baseline for the "Project Management 101" initiative. It is written so the same run can be pointed at the backend repo and the support repos.

items.title: What it produces
items.text:
One markdown file (docs/internal/architecture-overview.md by default) containing:

  • a summary and an "at a glance" table of modules and packages;
  • a Mermaid dependency graph (app → feature modules → internal packages → key third-party deps) and a Mermaid graph of runtime and network seams;
  • per-module and per-package sections: purpose, public API surface, seams, critical areas;
  • a ranked list of critical boundaries;
  • a table of third-party dependencies that need attention, with a risk rating;
  • build, CI and platform seams;
  • open questions for the project-management plan.

items.title: Shape of the run
items.text:
flowchart LR
  scout["Scout inline<br/>layout, LOC, pubspecs"] --> split["Split into<br/>~8-10 areas"]
  split --> readers
  subgraph readers["Read: parallel Sonnet agents, read-only"]
    r1["area 1"]
    r2["area 2"]
    rn["area N"]
  end
  readers --> synth["Synthesize: one Sonnet agent<br/>writes the doc, runs markdownlint"]
  synth --> verify["Verify: one Sonnet agent<br/>checks edges, paths, versions, fixes in place"]
  verify --> review["Human + Opus review,<br/>lint, commit locally"]
Phase Agents Model Writes files? Scout none, the main session session model no Read one per area, in parallel Sonnet no Synthesize 1 Sonnet only the output doc Verify 1 Sonnet only the output doc Review and commit none, the main session session model commit

The main session's model (Opus) does the scouting and the final review only. The readers and writers run on Sonnet: that is faster, and it keeps file dumps out of the main session's context, which only sees the finished document.

items.title: Step by step
items.text:
1. Branch. git checkout -b meat/project-management (or the repo's equivalent). Nothing is pushed until the doc has been reviewed.
  2. Scout inline to find out how to split the work:
  3. top-level layout and the module or package directories;
  4. LOC per directory, so that a very large module (here room, about 24k lines) is split across two readers, by concern (execution versus UI) rather than by folder;
  5. dependency manifests (pubspec.yaml, pyproject.toml, package.json);
  6. the markdown lint config, because the synthesizer has to satisfy it.
  7. Define the areas. Use 8 to 10 areas, each a scope (paths) plus a focus. Always include one area for third-party deps plus build, CI and deploy, with its own output headings (a dependency table with risk ratings).
  8. Run the workflow using the script below, with the areas passed in args.
  9. Review. Read the document, check the Mermaid diagrams render (GitHub preview or https://mermaid.live), run the linter, and commit locally.

items.title: Reader contract
items.text:
Every reader gets the same preamble, which keeps the notes uniform enough to merge:

  • read-only, and only claim what was seen in code;
  • fixed headings: Purpose, Public API surface, Dependencies (exact, grep the imports), Seams & boundaries (network, process, isolate, platform channel, storage, routing, DI, cross-module contracts, conditional imports), Critical / delicate areas, Size & test notes;
  • a cap of about 700 words.

The verify stage exists because readers summarise, and summaries drift. It re-checks each Mermaid edge against the real imports, checks that cited paths exist and that versions match the manifests, and checks the Mermaid syntax (unquoted parentheses in labels are the usual breakage).

items.title: Reusable script
items.text:
Pass it to the Workflow tool with args:

{
  "root": "/abs/path/to/repo",
  "repo": "soliplex (backend)",
  "asOf": "2026-10-09, main @ <sha>",
  "out": "docs/internal/architecture-overview.md",
  "lint": "npx markdownlint-cli2",
  "areas": [
    { "key": "api", "prompt": "Scope: src/soliplex/views/** — HTTP routes, auth deps, ..." },
    { "key": "deps-platform", "prompt": "Scope: third-party deps and build/CI. ..." }
  ]
}

export const meta = {
  name: 'architecture-map',
  description: 'Map modules, API surfaces, seams and risky deps of a repo into one markdown doc',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Read', model: 'sonnet' },
    { title: 'Synthesize', model: 'sonnet' },
    { title: 'Verify', model: 'sonnet' },
  ],
}

const { root, repo, asOf, out, lint, areas } = args
const OUT = `${root}/${out}`
const COMMON = `You are mapping the architecture of ${repo} at ${root} (read-only; do NOT edit files).
Report dense markdown notes, no preamble, under these headings:
## Purpose ## Public API surface ## Dependencies (exact; grep imports; internal + third-party)
## Seams & boundaries ## Critical / delicate areas (cite file:line) ## Size & test notes
Only claim what you saw in code. Under ~700 words.`

phase('Read')
const notes = (await parallel(areas.map(a => () =>
  agent(`${COMMON}\n\n${a.prompt}`, { label: `read:${a.key}`, phase: 'Read', model: 'sonnet' })
    .then(text => ({ key: a.key, text }))))).filter(Boolean)
log(`${notes.length}/${areas.length} readers returned`)

phase('Synthesize')
const bundle = notes.map(n => `\n\n===== NOTES: ${n.key} =====\n${n.text}`).join('')
await agent(`Write ${OUT} (the ONLY file you may write; create dirs). Technical, concise, ~350-500 lines.
Sections: title + summary ("as of ${asOf}"); at-a-glance table; Mermaid dependency flowchart
(layers as subgraphs, accurate edges only); Mermaid runtime/network seams diagram; optional
sequenceDiagram of the most critical path; per-module and per-package sections; ranked
"Critical boundaries"; "Third-party dependencies needing attention" table; "Build, CI &
platform seams"; "Open questions for the PM plan". Follow the repo's markdownlint config;
run \`cd ${root} && ${lint} ${out}\` until clean. Quote Mermaid labels with special chars.
Return a 5-line summary.${bundle}`, { label: 'synthesize', phase: 'Synthesize', model: 'sonnet' })

phase('Verify')
const verdict = await agent(`Fact-check ${OUT} against the code in ${root}: every Mermaid edge
(grep imports; flag important missing edges), cited paths exist, versions match manifests,
named classes/endpoints exist, Mermaid syntax valid. Fix in place (only that file), then run
\`cd ${root} && ${lint} ${out}\` until clean. Return corrections made and unverifiable claims.`,
  { label: 'verify', phase: 'Verify', model: 'sonnet' })

return { readers: notes.map(n => n.key), verdict }

items.title: Areas used for this repo
items.text: Key Scope shell lib/main*.dart, the library barrel, lib/src/{core,flavors,interfaces,shared,status_message} auth lib/src/modules/auth, packages/soliplex_client_native room-exec lib/src/modules/room, the non-visual parts: run, send/cancel, upload, filters room-ui lib/src/modules/room, the visual parts: markdown, LaTeX, highlighting, citations UI features lobby, quiz, versions, diagnostics modules agent packages/soliplex_agent client packages/soliplex_client: endpoints, AG-UI, schema drift design-logging packages/soliplex_design, packages/soliplex_logging, ADR-002/003 deps-platform all pubspecs, the lockfile, CI, Docker, nginx, platform folders

items.title: Adapting it to another repo
items.text:
• Python backend. Replace pubspec.yaml with pyproject.toml and the lockfile. Split readers by router or view, storage and DB layer, agent and tool runtime, and config. Use an api-surface reader that lists every route, and a deps-platform reader.
  • Small support repo (one package, under ~5k LOC). Three or four readers are enough. You can drop the verify stage only if a human checks every diagram edge.
  • Lint. Set lint to whatever the repo enforces (on this box markdownlint-cli2 is only reachable through npx), and tell the synthesizer which rules are disabled.
  • Cost. About 11 agents per run (9 readers, 1 synthesizer, 1 verifier). Readers are independent, so wall-clock time is roughly the slowest reader plus two sequential agents.

items.title: Outcome of the first run (2026-10-09)
items.text:
• 11 Sonnet agents (9 readers, 1 synthesizer, 1 verifier), all succeeded. The run took about 5 minutes and used about 750k subagent tokens. The output is a 425-line overview with three Mermaid diagrams.
  • The verify stage earned its keep. It found:
  • a reversed edge (diagnostics → room should have been room → diagnostics);
  • about eight missing edges;
  • two class names that do not exist (OidcDiscovery, ClassificationBadge);
  • wrong paths for the room screens (ui/ prefix missing);
  • a false "no tests" claim about secure storage.
  • Agents could not render Mermaid, so the review step rendered every block with npx --yes -p @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli mmdc -i x.mmd -o x.svg. All blocks passed. Add this to the verify prompt next time.
  • markdownlint-cli2 was not on PATH, so the agents fell back to npx. Pass lint: "npx markdownlint-cli2" up front.

items.title: Caveats
items.text:
• The output is a snapshot. Stamp it with the commit SHA and re-run it rather than hand-patching it once it has drifted.
  • Readers can over-generalise from one file. Treat risk ratings as prompts for discussion, not verdicts.
  • Keep the readers read-only. Only the synthesize and verify agents write, and only to the output file, so the run never touches source.

items.title: Soliplex Frontend Architecture Overview
items.text: As of 2026-10-09, main @ 67b846e3. Soliplex Frontend is a Flutter application and importable library (lib/soliplex_frontend.dart) for the Soliplex RAG/agent backend. A Flavor declares identity, theme and a list of AppModules; Flavor.build() lowers it to a ShellConfig that runSoliplexShell boots. Six feature modules (auth, lobby, room, quiz, diagnostics, versions) contribute routes, Riverpod overrides and redirects. They sit on five workspace packages (agent, client, client_native, design, logging). Riverpod is DI only; all reactive state is signals. The backend link is REST plus an AG-UI SSE stream. This document is the factual base for the "Project Management 101" plan. It was compiled from per-subsystem reads; items marked "not verified" were not confirmed in code.

items.title: At a glance
items.text: Unit Layer Purpose Approx LOC Criticality lib/src/core, flavors, shared, status_message Shell Module system, router, redirects, inactivity, storage migration, flavor assembly ~4.4k High lib/src/mockups Shell (dev) UI mockup harness (main_mockups.dart), excluded from coverage ~7.2k Low modules/auth Feature Multi-server OIDC, token refresh, secure storage, guards ~5.2k Critical modules/lobby Feature Server and room discovery, read markers ~3.8k Medium modules/room Feature Chat, threads, uploads, citations, execution timeline ~23.9k Critical modules/quiz Feature Room quizzes ~1.3k Low modules/diagnostics Feature HTTP/SSE inspector, log viewer, report export ~4.0k Medium (security) modules/versions Feature App and backend version display ~0.6k Low soliplex_agent Package (pure Dart) Agent runtime, run orchestration, tool registry ~6.1k Critical soliplex_client Package (pure Dart) REST and AG-UI SSE client, domain models, HTTP decorators ~15k Critical soliplex_client_native Package Per-platform SoliplexHttpClient ~0.75k High soliplex_design Package Tokens, themes, branded components ~3.9k Medium soliplex_logging Package (pure Dart) Loggers, sinks, describeFailure redaction ~2.1k High design_system/ Reference bundle HTML specimen and tokens.{css,dart,jsx}; must stay in sync with soliplex_design n/a Low
