    The rung's scripts come from the installed release, so walking a rung with a mismatched skill runs older scripts and generates an old-template reference: a comparison against it shows nothing to change. To check that the installed skill matches this page, ask its generator for its defaults: this page's release names the image tag, where an older one names the PyPI constraint instead:

    uv run <skill>/scripts/generate_soliplex_project.py --print-defaults \
    | grep -E 'soliplex_(image_tag|backend_constraint)'
#   "soliplex_image_tag": "0.85",

  2. Start from a clean git tree, on a branch of its own, so each step below is a commit you can review, and switching back to your usual branch undoes the lot. Tag the starting point too; section 2 compares against it:

    git status --short                     # should list nothing
git switch -c upgrade-soliplex-0.85
git tag pre-upgrade-soliplex-0.85

    A checkout cloned under src/ (e.g. a dev-mode src/soliplex) is its own repository, which the stack's .gitignore hides from git status, so check it separately:

    git -C src/soliplex status --short     # for each checkout under src/

  3. Stop the stack with docker compose down, and check that nothing is left running (a one-off docker compose run container, say):

    docker compose down
docker compose ps -a                   # should list nothing

    Never down -v here: that drops the Postgres volume holding the databases this upgrade migrates. (From step 5 on, docker compose ps -a also lists a stopped postgres container, which step 5 starts and stops again; that one is expected.)

  4. Record the state of each RAG store, to compare against after the upgrade. A stack whose docker-compose.yml has the one-shot haiku-rag service runs the CLI on it:

    docker compose run --rm haiku-rag info --db /data/haiku.rag.lancedb

    An older stack, without that service, runs it on the ingester instead. --no-deps keeps the ingester's dependencies (Postgres, docling-serve) stopped, and -e sets the queue password the config interpolates, which run would otherwise lose along with the ingester's own command; info never opens the queue, so any value will do:

    docker compose run --rm --no-deps -e INGESTER_DB_PASSWORD=unused \
    haiku-ingester haiku-rag info --db /data/haiku.rag.lancedb

    Run it once per store, rag/db/<stem>.lancedb appearing in the container as /data/<stem>.lancedb. Note the haiku.rag version (db) and the document and chunk counts.

  5. Back up the data the migrations touch, into a new directory under tmp/, which the stack's .gitignore already ignores. The directory is named to the second, so a second run makes a second backup: cp -a into a directory that already exists would nest the copy inside it instead. The Postgres dumps need Postgres running, and only Postgres:

    BACKUP=tmp/backup-$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S)
mkdir "$BACKUP"
docker compose up -d --wait postgres
for db in soliplex_agui soliplex_authz; do
    docker compose exec -T postgres sh -c \
        'PGPASSWORD=$(cat /run/secrets/postgres_password) \
         pg_dump -h localhost -U postgres -Fc "$0"' "$db" \
        > "$BACKUP/$db.dump"
done
docker compose stop postgres
cp -a rag/db "$BACKUP/rag-db"

    Then check the dumps: a failed pg_dump still leaves its output file behind, empty. Each should be non-empty and start with PGDMP:

    for f in "$BACKUP"/*.dump; do printf '%s: ' "$f"; head -c 5 "$f"; echo; done

    Use your own database names if they differ (the manifest's agui_db and authz_db).

  6. Take a dev-mode checkout off the path. If the backend's PYTHONPATH in docker-compose.yml lists a checkout providing the soliplex package (e.g. /app/src/soliplex/src), take it off for the upgrade:

    uv run <skill>/scripts/src_projects.py remove soliplex

    Ignore its closing advice to docker compose up -d backend: the stack stays down until the end of the section. remove also takes the checkout off the backend's watch list (its --reload-dirs), and settles an older reload mode: --reload=both becomes --reload=config, while --reload=python stays, being what turns reload on without watching the config (--reload=config would work as well).

    The checkout's code would otherwise override the soliplex the rebuilt image installs, and the migrations would ask the wrong release. Putting it back is the last step, Restore dev mode.

  7. Fetch the migration scripts if the stack's scripts/ lacks migrate_soliplex_dbs.py and migrate_rag_dbs.py (stacks generated before soliplex-template 0.17):

    for s in migrate_soliplex_dbs migrate_rag_dbs; do
    curl -fsSL -o "scripts/$s.py" \
        "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/soliplex/soliplex-template/main/scripts/$s.py"
done

    Each is a PEP 723 shim: uv run provisions the soliplex-template package from PyPI, which holds the migration code itself.

  8. Read the scripts' advice with the upgrade in mind. src_projects.py and both migration scripts end by telling you to start or restart a service. Mid-upgrade, ignore that: each section says when to bring the stack up.

<skill> is wherever the soliplex-template skill is installed, e.g. ~/.claude/skills/soliplex-template. The steps below edit the manifest in a few places, although its header says not to: they are the exception, so that it describes the stack the upgrade leaves.

items.title: Follow the upgrade steps for your rung
items.text:
Follow the steps listed for your upgrade rung in order. After each step, check the status of your stack's files:

git status

If there are changes, commit them with a short checkpoint commit message:

git add .
git commit -m "Step #2: <short description>"

items.title: Restore Dev mode
items.text:
A stack that ran a soliplex checkout in dev mode can put it back now; add puts it on the path and watches it, like any other project. Check out the release the image runs first: the checkout supplies only soliplex's code, and its dependencies still come from the image, so a checkout far from the image's release fails at import time.

docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend soliplex-cli --version
git -C src/soliplex checkout v<the version just reported>
uv run <skill>/scripts/src_projects.py add soliplex
docker compose up -d backend

items.title: Check it
items.text:
docker compose ps                    # every service running, backend healthy
docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend soliplex-cli audit /environment
ls backend/environment/rooms         # room ids, for the 'ask' below
docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend \
    soliplex-cli ask /environment <room-id> "Say hello"

For the upgrade, what matters in the audit is its database lines: both databases OK at the same Alembic revision. It can still exit non-zero for reasons of its own, such as models missing on the Ollama server (soliplex-cli ollama pull fetches them). The ask should return a reply and persist its thread. Open the frontend (http://localhost:9000 by default) for a last look.

items.title: Checking the whole stack against a reference
items.text:
For more than a smoke test, generate a throwaway stack from this stack's own generation manifest, with the skill release the rung walks with, and diff the two. The manifest under [tool.soliplex-template.params] records every parameter the stack was built with, so the reference is the stack as that release's generator would scaffold it:

cd <stack>

# Build a params file from the manifest. The generator recomputes derived
# values, so they are not accepted as input -- drop them. Manifests from
# before rung 7 also record 'auth_mode = "auth"', which the generator now
# refuses (providers are added after generation), so drop that too. (If it
# rejects others, its error message names them; add those to the list.)
python3 - <<'EOF' > /tmp/ref-params.json
import json, pathlib, tomllib

manifest = tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path("pyproject.toml").read_text())
params = manifest["tool"]["soliplex-template"]["params"]
for dropped in (
    "package_name",
    "frontend_release_path",
    "backend_auth_flag",
    "docling_serve_image",
    "auth_mode",
):
    params.pop(dropped, None)
print(json.dumps(params, indent=2))
EOF

uv run <skill>/scripts/generate_soliplex_project.py \
    --out /tmp/ref-stack --params /tmp/ref-params.json \
    --no-git --no-generate-secrets

Then diff the files the rung changed, e.g. for rung 0:

diff -u /tmp/ref-stack/pyproject.toml pyproject.toml
diff -ru /tmp/ref-stack/src src

Two differences are expected and harmless: skill_source_commit and skill_generated in the manifest record your stack's generation, and the reference's are blank or current. Anything else is a real divergence.

items.title: Afterwards
items.text:
The stack's own agent guide (AGENTS.md, or CLAUDE.md in older stacks) and its docs/ were written for the stack as generated, and the upgrade leaves them describing the old setup: backend/constraints.txt, the old image tags. Refresh them from a reference stack generated with your parameters (see the tip at the top), or at least treat them as out of date.

Wrap the run into main: merge the rung's branch and bring the live stack up on the merged state. What merges is the files; what rolls out is the state: the migration steps the rung rehearsed run live, against the deployment's own databases and stores.

  • In the live stack's clone, the merge is direct, and the rollout follows it in the same working tree.
  • From a separate upgrade-only clone, the clone is the rehearsal: it proved the rung's steps against copied stores and databases; push the branch and open the PR for the files, and roll out live afterwards by re-running the rung's migration steps for real.

items.title: Upgrade rungs
items.text:
One page per rung:

  • 0: Move to the src/ project layout
  • 1: Move to soliplex 0.85
  • 2: Build on the soliplex release images
  • 3: Move to soliplex 0.86.1 and haiku.rag 0.101.0
  • 4: Move to soliplex 0.87
  • 5: Serve through nginx
  • 6: Provision rooms on request
  • 7: OIDC providers and stack-init
  • 8: The provisioner on soliplex-concierge
  • 9: Room id forms and tracker labels
  • 10: Move to soliplex 0.93

items.title: Build on the soliplex release images
items.text:
Part of Upgrading an existing stack.

Walk this rung with the v0.18 skill release — its generator produces the rung's end state (the 0.85 release-image shape). The stack being upgraded names the release that generated it in its own [tool.soliplex-template] manifest — use that one when climbing from an older shape.

uv run <skill>/scripts/skill_versions.py upgrade v0.18

From here the backend no longer resolves soliplex from PyPI: it builds on the published ghcr.io/soliplex/soliplex-postgres image, which already holds soliplex and its PostgreSQL driver. See Backend image & dependencies for how the result works.

Stop the stack first (docker compose down). The backend reloads backend/environment/ as soon as a file there changes, so a running stack would pick up step 5's edit on the old image.

  1. Note your extras. The old backend/Dockerfile installs packages with uv add. Anything on that line other than soliplex, psycopg[binary], asyncpg, textual, textual-fspicker and textual-serve is yours, and so is any pin in backend/constraints.txt other than soliplex's. Your own edits to the two files show in their history from generation to the pre-upgrade tag, which leaves out section 1's changes:

    git diff $(git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD) pre-upgrade \
    -- backend/Dockerfile backend/constraints.txt

    That takes the stack's first commit as "as generated", which holds when the generator created the repository (its default). For a stack generated with --no-git, or whose history was rewritten, compare against a reference stack instead (see the tip at the top).

    The textual packages go: the backend image no longer carries the TUI's dependencies, so a TUI run inside the backend container needs the TUI service instead (include_tui).

  2. Create backend/requirements.txt with your extras, one requirement per line: an httpx2 on the uv add line with an httpx2 >= 2.16 pin in constraints.txt becomes the single line httpx2 >= 2.16. Drop pins on packages the soliplex release already holds: the build freezes the image's own versions as constraints, so a pin that disagrees fails the build rather than moving them. With no extras, the file holds only its header:

    # Extra PyPI dependencies for this stack's backend image, one requirement per
# line (pip requirements syntax), e.g.:
#
#   cowsay
#   httpx2-kerberos >= 2.1.1
#
# backend/Dockerfile installs them into the soliplex image's '/app/.venv',
# with every package the image already holds frozen as a constraint: an extra
# may add packages, but one that needs a different version of something the
# soliplex release pinned fails the build rather than moving it.
#
# Rebuild after editing: 'docker compose build backend' (add 'soliplex-dev'
# if you use dev mode, which builds its own copy of this image).
#
# Local projects under src/ are not installed from here; they are mounted
# and put on PYTHONPATH (see docs/users/custom-package.md).

  3. Replace backend/Dockerfile with the release-image one below. Carry over any local edits from step 1 (e.g. a COPY of vendor/).

    # syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# Built on the soliplex release image with PostgreSQL support: '/app/.venv'
# holds soliplex and its 'postgres' extra (pure-Python 'psycopg' over the
# image's system 'libpq5'). Its tag picks the release: a moving
# '<major>.<minor>' tag follows patch releases on
# 'docker compose build --pull backend'; an exact '<major>.<minor>.<patch>'
# pins one. Only what is particular to this stack is layered on below.
#
# The release image carries neither 'uv' nor 'bwrap': 'uv' is mounted for the
# build steps that need it (never copied into the image, as upstream does),
# and 'bwrap' is installed for the 'bubble-sandbox' skill.
FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.18 AS uv

FROM ghcr.io/soliplex/soliplex-postgres:0.85

WORKDIR /app

# Enable bytecode compilation for faster startup
ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 \
    UV_LINK_MODE=copy

# 'bwrap' for the 'bubble-sandbox' skill. Running code also needs the
# backend's 'security_opt' in docker-compose.yml (generator: enable_sandbox).
RUN \
  apt-get update && \
  apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    bubblewrap && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Extra PyPI dependencies for this stack, one requirement per line (see
# requirements.txt). The soliplex image's own versions are frozen as
# constraints, so an extra can add packages but never silently move one the
# release pinned; an extra that needs a different version fails the build
# instead. Skipped while the file holds only comments and blank lines.
COPY --link requirements.txt /tmp/requirements.txt

RUN --mount=from=uv,source=/uv,target=/usr/local/bin/uv \
    --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    if grep -qv '^[[:space:]]*\(#\|$\)' /tmp/requirements.txt; then \
      uv pip freeze --python /app/.venv/bin/python \
        > /tmp/base-constraints.txt && \
      uv pip install --python /app/.venv/bin/python \
        --constraints /tmp/base-constraints.txt \
        --requirements /tmp/requirements.txt; \
    fi

# Bootstrap sandbox environments
COPY --link sandbox/environments /sandbox/environments

RUN --mount=from=uv,source=/uv,target=/usr/local/bin/uv \
    --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    for env_dir in /sandbox/environments/*/; do \
      if [ -f "$env_dir/pyproject.toml" ]; then \
        uv --directory "$env_dir" sync --frozen; \
      fi; \
    done

# UID/GID the service runs as. Passed from docker-compose.yml (build.args),
# which sources PUID/PGID from .env; defaults match the historical 1000:1000.
# Aligning the image user with the host operator lets host-owned bind mounts
# and 0600 Docker secrets be read/written without a uid mismatch. (The
# soliplex image deliberately creates no user of its own.)
ARG PUID=1000
ARG PGID=1000
RUN groupadd -g ${PGID} soliplex && useradd -m -u ${PUID} -g ${PGID} soliplex

USER soliplex

ENV PATH="/app/.venv/bin:$PATH"

CMD ["/app/.venv/bin/soliplex-cli", "serve", "--host=0.0.0.0", "--proxy-headers", "--forwarded-allow-ips=*", "/environment"]

  4. Delete backend/constraints.txt.

  5. Switch the async driver in backend/environment/installation.yaml: both async_dburi values change postgresql+asyncpg:// to postgresql+psycopg://. The image ships psycopg, not asyncpg. Leave haiku.rag/haiku.rag.yaml alone: the haiku.rag image has its own driver, as the comment above its dburi says.

  6. Replace the backend's healthcheck test in docker-compose.yml. The image has no curl, so the test: entry under the backend's healthcheck: uses the venv's Python instead; keep its interval, timeout and retries:

        healthcheck:
      # The soliplex image has no curl; use the venv's stdlib instead.
      test:
        - "CMD"
        - "python"
        - "-c"
        - "import urllib.request,sys; sys.exit(0 if urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8000/api/ok', timeout=5).status == 200 else 1)"
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 4

    It takes effect when step 13 recreates the container.

  7. The TUI, if tui/Dockerfile exists: replace it with the one below, built FROM ghcr.io/soliplex/soliplex-tui at the same tag as the backend, and delete tui/constraints.txt:

    # syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# Built on the soliplex-tui release image: soliplex plus the TUI's
# dependencies (textual, textual-serve, textual-fspicker) in '/app/.venv'. It
# talks to the backend over HTTP, so it needs no PostgreSQL driver. It shares
# its tag with the backend's soliplex-postgres image, so the two always run
# the same soliplex release.
FROM ghcr.io/soliplex/soliplex-tui:0.85

WORKDIR /app

# UID/GID the service runs as (build.args from docker-compose.yml, sourced from
# PUID/PGID in .env; defaults to the historical 1000:1000). The soliplex-tui
# image deliberately creates no user of its own.
ARG PUID=1000
ARG PGID=1000
RUN groupadd -g ${PGID} soliplex && useradd -m -u ${PUID} -g ${PGID} soliplex

USER soliplex

ENV PATH="/app/.venv/bin:$PATH"

EXPOSE 8002

CMD ["/app/.venv/bin/soliplex-tui-serve"]

  8. Update the stack's host-side dependencies in the root pyproject.toml. The soliplex, psycopg[binary] and asyncpg entries become one:

    dependencies = [
    "soliplex[postgres-binary] >= 0.85, < 0.86",
]

    then refresh the lock and the environment (uv lock && uv sync). Section 1 already moved the lock to 0.85, so the diff is small, mostly asyncpg dropping out. src/<package>/pyproject.toml already admits 0.85 (section 1, step 1).

  9. Update the manifest's parameters in the [tool.soliplex-template.params] table. The version parameters are renamed, soliplex_backend_constraint and soliplex_tui_constraint giving way to:

    soliplex_image_tag = "0.85"
soliplex_dev_constraint = ">= 0.85, < 0.86"

    and, if section 1 did not already set them, haiku_rag_version = "0.96.1" and enable_sandbox (section 1, steps 3 and 7). Finally, so the manifest names the template the stack now matches, set its skill_source_commit and skill_generated to the upgraded skill's own source_commit and generated, from the metadata: at the top of its SKILL.md. Only a built release carries that block: the skill as it sits in the template repository has none. A skill built from a checkout with scripts/build_skill.py gets one, stamped with the checkout's HEAD, which does not cover changes not yet committed there.

  10. Watch your own package. A stack generated before the backend watched its package carries no --reload-dirs, so an edit under src/<package>/ needs a restart. Have it watched, as a newly generated stack's is:

    uv run <skill>/scripts/src_projects.py add <package>

    Its PYTHONPATH entry is already there (unchanged); add adds the matching --reload-dirs=/app/src/<package>/src to the serve command. Ignore its advice to bring the backend up: step 13 does that.

  11. Give soliplex-dev a build of its own (stacks whose docker-compose.yml has a soliplex-dev service). It now builds on the backend's image plus every src/ project's dev dependency group, so a project's tests run there against the backend's versions, without the backend image carrying them. Make a soliplex-dev/ directory, save the template's Dockerfile into it as soliplex-dev/Dockerfile:

    # syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# The dev-mode 'soliplex-dev' service: the backend's own image (compose passes
# it as the 'backend' build context, 'service:backend'), plus the 'dev'
# dependency group of every project under src/ -- pytest and the like -- so a
# project's tests run against the very versions the backend imports it with.
#
# Those are listed in requirements-dev.txt, which src_projects.py generates
# from the projects' pyproject.toml files. They are installed with the backend
# image's own versions frozen as constraints, as backend/requirements.txt is: a
# dev requirement that needs a different version fails this build. Skipped
# while the file holds only comments and blank lines.
#
# The 'uv' tag is the one backend/Dockerfile mounts; keep the two in step.
FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.18 AS uv

FROM backend

# The backend image runs as the 'soliplex' user; installing needs root.
USER root

COPY --link requirements-dev.txt /tmp/requirements-dev.txt

RUN --mount=from=uv,source=/uv,target=/usr/local/bin/uv \
    --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    if grep -qv '^[[:space:]]*\(#\|$\)' /tmp/requirements-dev.txt; then \
      uv pip freeze --python /app/.venv/bin/python \
        > /tmp/base-constraints.txt && \
      uv pip install --python /app/.venv/bin/python \
        --constraints /tmp/base-constraints.txt \
        --requirements /tmp/requirements-dev.txt; \
    fi

USER soliplex

    then generate its requirements file from the projects' dev groups:

    uv run <skill>/scripts/src_projects.py dev-requirements

    and point the service's build: at it, in place of its context: backend, dockerfile: Dockerfile and args::

        build:
      context: soliplex-dev
      additional_contexts:
        backend: "service:backend"

    Commit both files. Step 13 builds it.

  12. Build nginx on the published web client. Instead of building the Flutter client from a release tarball, nginx/Dockerfile now copies it from the ghcr.io/soliplex/frontend-web image, already cache-busted. Replace the Dockerfile with the template's, keeping your own -subj "…" certificate subject on its openssl req line:

    # The built Soliplex web client, published by soliplex/frontend as an image
# holding only 'build/web', already cache-busted: everything but index.html,
# the manifest, favicon and icons sits under a 'v<release-tag>/' directory,
# with relative URLs, so the same tree serves under any '<base href>'. Its tag
# picks the release: a moving '<major>.<minor>' tag follows patch releases on
# 'docker compose build --pull nginx'; an exact '<major>.<minor>.<patch>' (or
# '<major>.<minor>.<patch>-<build>') pins one.
FROM ghcr.io/soliplex/frontend-web:0.110 AS frontend

FROM debian:trixie

# UID/GID the service runs as (build.args from docker-compose.yml, sourced from
# PUID/PGID in .env; defaults to the historical 1000:1000). Used below to own
# the build-time self-signed TLS material and create the runtime user.
ARG PUID=1000
ARG PGID=1000

# Install:
# - iputils-ping for network debugging
# - openssl for certificate generation,
# - ca-certificates
# - curl for healthcheck
# - headers-more module to suppress the Server header
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install --no-install-recommends -y \
        openssl ca-certificates curl \
        libnginx-mod-http-headers-more-filter \
        libnginx-mod-http-ndk \
        libnginx-mod-http-lua && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Generate self-signed SSL certificate
RUN mkdir -p /etc/nginx/ssl && \
    openssl req -x509 -nodes -days 365 -newkey rsa:2048 \
    -keyout /etc/nginx/ssl/server.key \
    -out /etc/nginx/ssl/server.crt \
    -subj "/C=US/ST=State/L=City/O=Organization/CN=localhost" && \
    chown -R ${PUID}:${PGID} /etc/nginx/ssl

ENV SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
ENV SSL_CERT_DIR=/etc/ssl/certs
ENV REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt

# The built web client, served from here (see nginx.conf)
COPY --from=frontend /build/web /app/build/web

# nginx configuration (nginx.conf, mime.types, error-pages) is bind-mounted
# from the host at runtime (see docker-compose.yml), so edits don't require
# an image rebuild.

EXPOSE 9000 9443
RUN groupadd -g ${PGID} soliplex && useradd -m -u ${PUID} -g ${PGID} soliplex
USER soliplex
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --retries=3 \
    CMD curl -f http://localhost:9000/ || exit 1

CMD ["nginx", "-g", "daemon off;"]

    delete nginx/post-build-cache-bust.sh, which it no longer runs, and in nginx/nginx.conf replace the hashed-asset locations — in both server blocks, the HTTP one and the HTTPS one — with the one below. The image names its asset directory for the release tag, build metadata included (v0.110.0+96/), which the old pattern does not match, so without this change the assets lose their long-lived caching:

            location ~ "^/v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(\+[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?/(.*)" {
            expires 1y;
            add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable";
        }

    Then, in the manifest, set frontend_version to the image tag (0.110 follows the 0.110 series) and drop frontend_release_path, which nothing reads any more.

  13. Tag the current backend image, then rebuild with --pull, so Docker fetches the release image, and bring the stack up:

    docker tag <project>-backend:latest <project>-backend:pre-release-image
docker compose build --pull backend nginx
docker compose up -d

    Tag and rebuild tui the same way if the stack has it, and add soliplex-dev to the build if the stack has that (it builds on the backend's image). Then Check it, and commit.
path: Build on the soliplex release images

items.title: Move to soliplex 0.85
items.text:
Part of Upgrading an existing stack.

Walk this rung with the v0.18b1 skill release — its generator produces the rung's end state (Soliplex 0.85 built from PyPI; uv add-shaped). The stack being upgraded names the release that generated it in its own [tool.soliplex-template] manifest — use that one when climbing from an older shape.

uv run <skill>/scripts/skill_versions.py upgrade v0.18b1

This section keeps the stack's PyPI-built backend/Dockerfile; only versions and configuration shapes change. Skip the steps that do not apply.

  1. Raise the soliplex pin, everywhere the stack has one:

    • backend/constraints.txt, and tui/constraints.txt if the stack has the TUI:

      soliplex >= 0.85, < 0.86

    • the soliplex entry in the root pyproject.toml's dependencies ("soliplex >= 0.85, < 0.86");

    • the soliplex requirement in src/<package>/pyproject.toml. That is your own library, so check rather than overwrite: if the range it gives does not admit 0.85, raise it to >= 0.85, < 0.86.

    Then refresh both lock files and the host environment, so host-side work runs 0.85 from here on:

    uv lock && uv sync
(cd src/<package> && uv lock && uv sync)

    Expect large lock diffs: the new soliplex pulls in a newer dependency tree.

  2. Add bubblewrap to the apt-get install list in backend/Dockerfile, whether or not any room uses the sandbox skill yet: soliplex 0.84 and later refuse a room configuring that skill unless bwrap can run, and the current template always installs it. (A stack going on to section 2 replaces this Dockerfile there, so it may skip this step.)

  3. Bump the haiku.rag image to ghcr.io/ggozad/haiku.rag-slim:0.96.1, in both places it appears: the FROM line of haiku.rag/Dockerfile, and the haiku-ingester service's image: in docker-compose.yml (in newer stacks that line also carries an &haiku_rag_image anchor; keep it). soliplex 0.85 requires haiku.rag-slim >= 0.96.1, < 0.97, and the ingester writes the stores the backend reads. Record the new version in the manifest:

    haiku_rag_version = "0.96.1"

    The template's two haiku.rag.yaml files need no changes between haiku.rag 0.82 and 0.96.1. For a later bump, check haiku.rag's release notes for configuration changes.

  4. Bump docling-serve to v1.32.0, in docling-serve/Dockerfile and the docling-serve service's image: (and the commented GPU alternatives beside each). It goes with the haiku.rag bump: v1.32.0 carries the docling stack haiku.rag 0.83 and later pin. It changes no stored data, but it does change how documents re-ingested from now on are chunked, and so their chunk ids; see Converter bumps.

  5. Rename the database settings (stacks from before soliplex 0.82, whose installation.yaml still has thread_persistence_dburi:). Each section gets a new name, and its keys a _dburi suffix:

    thread_persistence_db:
  sync_dburi: "postgresql+psycopg://soliplex_agui:secret:AGUI_DB_PASSWORD@postgres/soliplex_agui"
  async_dburi: "postgresql+asyncpg://soliplex_agui:secret:AGUI_DB_PASSWORD@postgres/soliplex_agui"

authorization_db:
  sync_dburi: "postgresql+psycopg://soliplex_authz:secret:AUTHZ_DB_PASSWORD@postgres/soliplex_authz"
  async_dburi: "postgresql+asyncpg://soliplex_authz:secret:AUTHZ_DB_PASSWORD@postgres/soliplex_authz"

    Rename the commented SQLite alternatives (#sync:, #async:) the same way, so uncommenting one later does not bring the old spelling back. Keep your own role and database names if they differ. (Section 2 later switches the async_dburi driver to psycopg.)

  6. Update sandbox rooms. List the rooms that configure the sandbox skill:

    grep -rln 'kind: "\(bubble-sandbox\|bwrap_sandbox\)"' backend/environment/rooms

    soliplex 0.84 flattened the skill's settings, and rejects the old keys, so in each room listed:

    Before After default_environment: "bare" environment: "bare" allowed_environments: [...] (gone: the room runs one environment, and the model does not choose it) sandbox_config: → execution_timeout_seconds: 30 execution_timeout_seconds: 30.0 (top level) sandbox_config: → max_output_chars: 100000 max_output_chars: 10000 (top level)

  7. Add the sandbox security_opt block to the backend service in docker-compose.yml, after its user: line (where the template has it), and security_opt: *sandbox_security_opt to soliplex-dev if the stack has one. Add it live if a room from step 6 is to run code:

        security_opt: &sandbox_security_opt
      - seccomp=unconfined
      - apparmor=unconfined
      - systempaths=unconfined

    and commented out otherwise, as a stack generated today without the sandbox carries it, so opting in later means uncommenting it:

        #security_opt: &sandbox_security_opt
    #  - seccomp=unconfined
    #  - apparmor=unconfined
    #  - systempaths=unconfined

    add_room.py checks for the live block, and refuses to add a sandbox room to a stack without it. Record the choice in the manifest's [tool.soliplex-template.params] table, beside include_tui:

    enable_sandbox = false    # true with the live block

    Configuration explains what the block lifts and why.

  8. Add the one-shot haiku-rag service if docker-compose.yml lacks it: migrate_rag_dbs.py runs on it. It shares the ingester's settings through YAML anchors, so first name four of the haiku-ingester service's own keys, the ones directly under haiku-ingester: at its four-space indent (other services have keys of the same names; leave those alone):

      haiku-ingester:
    image: &haiku_rag_image ghcr.io/ggozad/haiku.rag-slim:0.96.1
    # ...
    volumes: &haiku_rag_volumes
    # ...
    environment: &haiku_rag_environment
    # ...
    ulimits: &haiku_rag_ulimits

    then add the service after it:

      haiku-rag:
    profiles: ["tools"]
    image: *haiku_rag_image
    build:
      context: haiku.rag
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    entrypoint:
      - sh
      - -c
      - |
        export INGESTER_DB_PASSWORD="$$(cat /run/secrets/ingester_db_password)"
        exec haiku-rag --config /app/haiku.rag.yaml "$$@"
      - haiku-rag
    volumes: *haiku_rag_volumes
    environment: *haiku_rag_environment
    user: "${PUID:-1000}:${PGID:-1000}"
    secrets:
      - ingester_db_password
    ulimits: *haiku_rag_ulimits

    Check it by running the CLI on it. It is held out of docker compose up by its profile, so plain docker compose config does not list it, but run enables the profile itself; against the new haiku.rag image this also reports any store migrations step 11 will apply:

    docker compose run --rm haiku-rag info --db /data/haiku.rag.lancedb

  9. Tag the current backend image, then rebuild. The tag keeps the old image to return to if the upgrade goes wrong; <project> is the name: at the top of docker-compose.yml:

    docker tag <project>-backend:latest <project>-backend:pre-soliplex-0.85
docker compose build --no-cache backend
docker compose build haiku-ingester docling-serve

    (and tag and rebuild tui the same way, if the stack has it). --no-cache matters: the backend resolves soliplex from PyPI in a cached layer, and without it Docker can reuse a layer an earlier build resolved, silently installing an older 0.85.x than the newest. To roll back, switch back to your usual branch and tag the old image as latest again; a database already migrated (step 10) also needs its backup restored.

  10. Migrate the Soliplex databases, with only Postgres running (the script runs the rebuilt backend image in a throwaway container, and refuses while the backend service is up). Databases created by soliplex 0.81 or earlier carry no Alembic stamp, and the backend refuses to start on them until stamped:

    docker compose up -d --wait postgres
uv run scripts/migrate_soliplex_dbs.py --check
uv run scripts/migrate_soliplex_dbs.py

    Stamping prints the bootstrap script's own advice to run soliplex-cli database upgrade; the script then runs it itself, so there is nothing to do by hand. A second --check should report both databases at head.

    Do this before section 2. Releases of the script up to soliplex-template 0.17.x fetch soliplex's stamping step with curl inside the backend image, which this PyPI-built image has and the release images do not.

  11. Migrate the RAG stores, with the ingester still stopped:

    uv run scripts/migrate_rag_dbs.py --check
uv run scripts/migrate_rag_dbs.py

    haiku.rag prints a warning that it is outdated, naming a newer release; ignore it, since soliplex 0.85 requires a release below 0.97. rag/db/ is ignored by git, so this step leaves nothing to commit.

  12. Bring the stack up (docker compose up -d), Check it, and commit.

Database migrations covers both migration scripts, and what their reports mean, in full.

items.title: Move to soliplex 0.86.1 and haiku.rag 0.101.0
items.text:
Part of Upgrading an existing stack.

Walk this rung with the v0.19b1 skill release — its generator produces the rung's end state (soliplex 0.86.1 on the release images, with haiku.rag 0.101.0). The stack being upgraded names the release that generated it in its own [tool.soliplex-template] manifest — use that one when climbing from an older shape.

uv run <skill>/scripts/skill_versions.py upgrade v0.19b1

  1. Stop backend and haiku-ingester, and back up the Postgres databases and rag/db/ before upgrading.

  2. Adopt the image-shape changes, which came to the template ahead of this step: the image shim Dockerfiles (haiku.rag/Dockerfile, docling-serve/Dockerfile) are gone; their build recipes moved to README.md files beside their build contexts, and the template's build: stanzas for those services ship commented. Delete your copies (or rename them to the README.mds, which carry the recipes), and comment the stanzas the same way.

  3. Set the backend and optional TUI image tags to 0.86.1; set the haiku.rag image to 0.101.0 in the haiku_rag_image anchor in docker-compose.yml; set the docling-serve image to quay.io/docling-project/docling-serve-cpu:v1.38.0.

  4. Update soliplex_image_tag, haiku_rag_version, and soliplex_dev_constraint in the project's manifest. Use >= 0.86.1, < 0.87 for the Soliplex requirement in the root and package pyproject.toml files, then run uv lock in each project.

  5. In haiku.rag/haiku.rag.yaml, move the source list from ingester.sources to the sources list of the ingester.databases entry keyed haiku.rag (the key is the database's own name, dot included). Keep its source ids and paths. Add namespace: soliplex under ingester.queue. This still writes /data/haiku.rag.lancedb. Additional databases are described in RAG pipeline.

  6. In the haiku-ingester Compose command, change sh -c to sh -ec and insert this command after exporting INGESTER_DB_PASSWORD and before exec haiku-ingester --config /app/haiku.rag.yaml serve:

    haiku-ingester --config /app/haiku.rag.yaml queue migrate

  7. Rebuild backend, soliplex-dev, haiku-ingester, docling-serve, and the optional tui with docker compose build --pull.

  8. Before restarting the ingester, follow the queue migration to migrate the schema and assign existing rows to soliplex. Otherwise the ingester will not see its previous jobs and sync state. The template prepares the queue schema before every ingester start. Manual namespace assignment is needed only when upgrading rows from a queue without namespaces.

  9. The ingester's new database API is GET /databases/{name}; update any callers of GET /database to follow suit.

  10. Run uv run scripts/migrate_soliplex_dbs.py --check and uv run scripts/migrate_rag_dbs.py --check; apply any reported migrations with the relevant service stopped. Start the stack with docker compose up -d and inspect the backend and ingester logs. Then Check it, and commit.

items.title: Move to soliplex 0.87
items.text:
Part of Upgrading an existing stack.

Walk this rung with the v0.19b2 skill release — its generator produces the rung's end state (soliplex 0.87.0 on the release images, with haiku.rag 0.101.0). The stack being upgraded names the release that generated it in its own [tool.soliplex-template] manifest — use that one when climbing from an older shape.

uv run <skill>/scripts/skill_versions.py upgrade v0.19b2

  1. Stop the stack with docker compose down, and back up the Postgres databases and rag/db/ before upgrading.

  2. This rung is a pure release bump: the upgrade changes no template files beyond version spellings, sets up no database migrations (the last alembic migrations shipped with soliplex v0.86), and leaves the haiku.rag pair and docling-serve untouched. Stacks that changed the generated files by hand should compare the rung's cut with the one their manifest names to confirm nothing else moved.

  3. Bump the baked soliplex image tags from 0.86.1 to 0.87.0: the FROM lines in backend/Dockerfile (ghcr.io/soliplex/soliplex-postgres) and, if the stack ships the TUI, tui/Dockerfile (ghcr.io/soliplex/soliplex-tui). If AGENTS.md or docs/architecture/backend.md name the release version, update those spellings to match.

  4. Update soliplex_image_tag and soliplex_dev_constraint in the project's manifest. Use >= 0.87.0, < 0.88 for the Soliplex requirement in the root and package pyproject.toml files, then run uv lock in each project.

  5. Rebuild backend, soliplex-dev, and the optional tui with docker compose build --pull.

  6. The default generated stack sets no migration policy, so the backend migrates its Alembic databases itself on startup. Stacks which configured a migration policy are responsible for driving their own migrations; the migrations reference describes running them with the CLI.

  7. Start the stack with docker compose up -d and inspect the backend logs. Then Check it, and commit.

items.title: Move to soliplex 0.93
items.text:
Part of Upgrading an existing stack.

Walk this rung with the v0.24 skill release — its generator produces the rung's end state. The stack being upgraded names the release that generated it in its own [tool.soliplex-template] manifest — use that one when climbing from an older shape.

uv run <skill>/scripts/skill_versions.py upgrade v0.24

This rung moves the stack to soliplex 0.93, haiku.rag-slim 0.112.0 and the 0.117 web client. What changes:

  • the releases: soliplex from the moving 0.89 image tag to 0.93, and the ingester from haiku.rag-slim 0.104.0 to 0.112.0; soliplex brings two Alembic migrations (thread labels in 0.92, full-text thread search in 0.93), which the backend applies itself on startup, and haiku.rag brings no RAG store migration
  • docling-serve: v1.38.0 to v1.38.2, the release haiku.rag 0.107 and later pair docling with
  • the web client: frontend 0.114 to 0.117, whose thread labels and thread search need soliplex 0.92 or later, so bump the two together
  • the image builds bind-mount the requirements files instead of copying them into /tmp: a COPY --link into /tmp leaves it mode 0755 under Docker's containerd image store, the default for new Docker 29 installs, which breaks apt in the soliplex-dev build and temporary files at run time
  • the soliplex-template floor in soliplex-dev/Dockerfile is >=0.22, as rung 9 set it; stacks generated by v0.22 or v0.23 still say >=0.21
  • the session key (SESSION_MIDDLEWARE_TOKEN) is a generated Docker secret, so sessions survive a backend restart; before, it fell back to a random value on every start
  • the sample bare-bones filesystem skill gains a body line, so soliplex-cli audit no longer flags it as having no instructions

Skip the steps that do not apply. Each names what the current template has; compare against a stack the rung's release generates.

  1. Stop the stack with docker compose down, and back up the Postgres databases and rag/db/ (see Before you start): this rung migrates both Soliplex databases.

  2. Bump the releases.

    • the FROM line in backend/Dockerfile: soliplex-postgres:0.89 becomes soliplex-postgres:0.93 (and in tui/Dockerfile, if the stack ships the TUI, soliplex-tui:0.89 becomes soliplex-tui:0.93)
    • the ingester image in docker-compose.yml (the &haiku_rag_image anchor): haiku.rag-slim:0.104.0 becomes haiku.rag-slim:0.112.0
    • the docling-serve image in docker-compose.yml: the v1.38.0 tag becomes v1.38.2 (for example docling-serve-cpu:v1.38.2)
    • the FROM line in nginx/Dockerfile: frontend-web:0.114 becomes frontend-web:0.117
    • the manifest in pyproject.toml: soliplex_image_tag = "0.93", soliplex_dev_constraint = ">= 0.93, < 0.94", haiku_rag_version = "0.112.0", docling_serve_version = "v1.38.2", the v1.38.2 tag in docling_serve_image, and frontend_version = "0.117"
    • the soliplex requirement in the root and package pyproject.toml files: >= 0.93, < 0.94; then run uv lock in each project that has a uv.lock (usually the root only)

    The two /v0.114.0+101/ examples in nginx/nginx.conf's comments become /v0.117.0+106/; nothing else in that file changes.

  3. Bind-mount the requirements files. In backend/Dockerfile, remove the line

    COPY --link requirements.txt /tmp/requirements.txt

    and add a bind mount to the RUN step that reads the file, after its two existing --mount lines:

    RUN --mount=from=uv,source=/uv,target=/usr/local/bin/uv \
    --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    --mount=type=bind,source=requirements.txt,target=/tmp/requirements.txt \
    if grep -qv '^[[:space:]]*\(#\|$\)' /tmp/requirements.txt; then \

    Do the same in soliplex-dev/Dockerfile for requirements-dev.txt: remove its COPY --link requirements-dev.txt /tmp/requirements-dev.txt line, and add --mount=type=bind,source=requirements-dev.txt,target=/tmp/requirements-dev.txt to the RUN step that follows it. The rest of each step is unchanged; the reference stack also carries a short comment above each step saying why the file is mounted.

    In the same file, check the soliplex-template floor. Rung 9 raised it, but the v0.22 and v0.23 generators did not, so a stack they generated may still have >=0.21:

    ARG SOLIPLEX_TEMPLATE="soliplex-template[provisioner]>=0.22"

  4. Make the session key a generated secret. In docker-compose.yml, declare it beside the other .gen secrets at the end of the file:

        session_middleware_token:
      file: ./.secrets/session_middleware_token.gen

    and add - session_middleware_token to two secrets: lists: the backend service's, and the one anchored &soliplex_dev_secrets on soliplex-dev, which soliplex-provisioner and stack-init share. In backend/environment/installation.yaml, put a file_path source first in SESSION_MIDDLEWARE_TOKEN's list:

      - secret_name: "SESSION_MIDDLEWARE_TOKEN"
    sources:
      - kind: "file_path"
        file_path: /run/secrets/session_middleware_token
      - kind: "env_var"
        env_var_name: "SOLIPLEX_SESSION_MIDDLEWARE_TOKEN"
      - kind: "random_chars"

    Then generate the new secret; the script writes only missing files:

    uv run scripts/generate_secrets.py

    Sessions signed with the old random key end once more when the backend first starts with this one.

  5. Give the sample skill a body. If the stack still has the generated backend/environment/skills/bare-bones/SKILL.md, add a line after its closing ---:

    Do nothing 'til you hear from me.

  6. Check the configuration you changed by hand. The generated files need nothing more, but soliplex 0.91 to 0.93 refuse some older spellings:

    • installation.yaml: the top-level thread_persistence_dburi: and authorization_dburi: stanzas are gone (since 0.91); use thread_persistence_db: and authorization_db:, each with sync_dburi and async_dburi
    • room and agent configs: a system_prompt or logo_image file must resolve inside the config's own directory (since 0.92)
    • OIDC providers: accepted_azp_list still loads, but is deprecated in favor of accepted_client_ids and goes away after 0.94
    • haiku.rag hooks and metadata providers: from 0.112, only edit_document writes a document's metadata["user"]; a user key set anywhere else is dropped

  7. Rebuild the images, the profiled soliplex-dev and stack-init included:

    docker compose --profile '*' build --pull

    docker compose up pulls the new ingester and docling-serve images itself.

  8. Check the databases. The Soliplex databases are behind by the two migrations above; with the default configuration the backend applies them when it starts. To see what is owed first:

    uv run scripts/migrate_soliplex_dbs.py --check

    A stack that configured a migration policy drives its own migrations; see the migrations reference. The RAG stores need nothing: no haiku.rag release since 0.91 changed their layout, so this should report nothing to migrate:

    uv run scripts/migrate_rag_dbs.py --check

    One exception: haiku.rag 0.112 no longer upgrades a store recorded before 0.64. A stack that has run its migrations at every rung has none; if --check reports one, migrate it with haiku.rag 0.111.1 first, as the error message says.

  9. Start the stack with docker compose up -d, then Check it, and commit. The audit's secrets section should list SESSION_MIDDLEWARE_TOKEN OK (file_path); with random_chars instead, it also warns that the value changes on every restart, which means step 4 is incomplete.

items.title: Move to the src/ project layout
items.text:
Part of Upgrading an existing stack.

Walk this rung with the v0.16.2 skill release — the release whose generator produces the rung's end state, and whose migrate_layout.py performs it.

uv run <skill>/scripts/skill_versions.py upgrade v0.16.2

Stacks generated before soliplex-template v0.16 put the project's package directly under src/, with its tests at the stack root:

<stack>/
  pyproject.toml
  src/<package>/            # tools.py, views.py
  tests/unit/

src/ was therefore one specific package rather than "the source trees", which left nowhere to put a second one. Newly generated stacks instead make every entry under src/ a project directory of the same shape:

<stack>/
  pyproject.toml            # stack tooling only
  src/
    <package>/              # this project
      pyproject.toml
      src/<package>/        # tools.py, views.py
      tests/unit/
    <other>/                # anything you clone alongside it

Every later rung assumes the new layout (rung 1, for instance, locks src/<package>/pyproject.toml), so a stack still in the old one starts here. The rung moves files only: it changes no database, RAG store, pin, or image.
path: Move to the src/ project layout

items.title: Use the script
items.text:
Ask the agent

Do not do this by hand. The skill ships scripts/migrate_layout.py, which performs every step of Doing it by hand and asserts on the text it expects to find at each one. It reads the package name from this stack's own [tool.soliplex-template.params], moves the tree with git mv so history follows as renames, splits pyproject.toml (keeping the stack's own soliplex constraint), repoints the backend's PYTHONPATH, and appends the src/ ignore rule. Nothing is written until every check has passed, so a stack that has drifted from the exemplar aborts intact — it names the file and the anchor it could not find, rather than leaving you half-converted.

  1. Show the plan, from the stack directory:

    uv run <skill>/scripts/migrate_layout.py --dry-run

  2. Apply it. It requires the clean git checkout that Before you start set up, so the result is reviewable as a diff (--force waives that, and moves files without git mv):

    uv run <skill>/scripts/migrate_layout.py

    If it reports a drifted file, reconcile that one file by hand, using the matching step of Doing it by hand, and re-run.

  3. Verify both halves. The library, from its own project directory, and the stack root, which is the half a hand migration usually breaks:

    (cd src/<package> && uv sync && uv run pytest)
uv sync && uv run zensical build

  4. Start the stack with docker compose up -d, so the backend picks up the new PYTHONPATH. Ask the custom room to greet someone, which exercises the dotted <package>.tools.greeting name through it:

    docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend \
    soliplex-cli ask /environment custom "Greet Alice"

    Then Check it, and commit.

  5. Tidy the loose ends, at your leisure: the dotted names in backend/environment/ do not change, but comments in installation.yaml and backend/environment/rooms/custom/room_config.yaml still point at the old paths.

The rest of this page documents what the script does, step by step. Read it if the script reported a drifted file and you need to reconcile that step by hand — or if you would simply rather see the work.
path: Move to the src/ project layout

items.title: Doing it by hand
items.text:
Changed your mind? Ordinary git cleanup hands it back to the script

The script converts a stack in one shot and refuses one that is already part-way there — a hand migration abandoned after step 1 reports has no src/<package>/tools.py, because the move it looks for has already happened. You do not have to finish by hand: every step below edits only tracked files, so the usual cleanup returns the stack to a state the script can take from the top.

cd <stack>
git reset --hard     # undo the moves and the edited files
git clean -fd        # drop files the migration newly created

Leave -x / -X off. Both would also delete ignored files, and in a generated stack that means .env, the .secrets/*.gen files (which Postgres has already been initialised against), the LanceDB under rag/db/, and every .venv.

The flip side is that ignored files do not travel back: build artifacts such as __pycache__/ or .pytest_cache/ stay wherever the half-finished move left them, and the migration will carry them along into the new tree — harmless, but it leaves a stray tests/ inside your package. Delete them before re-running:

find src -name __pycache__ -type d -prune -exec rm -rf {} +
git status --short   # must be empty before you re-run the script

This assumes the hand migration is uncommitted. If you committed it, git revert or reset to the commit before it, then clean as above.
path: Move to the src/ project layout

items.title: 1. Move the files
items.text:
Four git mvs, which git records as pure renames — history follows:

mkdir -p .mig/<package>
git mv src .mig/<package>
git mv tests .mig/<package>
git mv .mig src

Check it before going further:

git status --short     # every line should start with R

The intermediate needs the package-name level

mkdir .mig && git mv .mig src (without /<package>) lands the files at src/src/<package>/ and src/tests/, which is not the target layout. This is the first of the two steps that are easy to get wrong by hand; the pyproject.toml split below is the other.
path: Move to the src/ project layout

items.title: 2. Split pyproject.toml
items.text:
There are now two pyproject.toml files, and the split is not a pure move: only the build backend and the package/test settings migrate. The stack root keeps its [project] table, its dependency groups, and the [tool.soliplex-template] manifest — it stops being a distribution, not a project.

The stack root becomes exactly this (the [tool.soliplex-template] block already there stays put, unchanged, at the end):

[project]
name = "<project_name>"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
# Host-side dependencies for driving *the stack*.
dependencies = [
    "soliplex[postgres-binary] >= 0.85, < 0.86",
]

# Nothing at the stack root is importable, so there is nothing to build here.
[tool.uv]
package = false

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    # Builds the documentation site under docs/ (`uv run zensical build`).
    "zensical",
]

[tool.soliplex-template]
# ... the generation manifest, left exactly as it was ...

Keep [project] and [dependency-groups]

Deleting them along with [build-system] leaves the root with nothing but [tool.uv] and the manifest. uv sync then warns No requires-python value found in the workspace and uv run zensical build fails with Failed to spawn: zensical — the docs site has no tooling environment to run in. Step 5 below catches this.

Then create src/<package>/pyproject.toml with the parts you removed:

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "<project_name>"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
dependencies = ["soliplex >= 0.85, < 0.86"]

[dependency-groups]
dev = ["pytest"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/<package>"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests/unit"]
pythonpath = ["src"]

Leave the [tool.soliplex-template] manifest at the stack root: it records how the stack was generated, not how the library is built.
path: Move to the src/ project layout

items.title: 3. Repoint the backend's PYTHONPATH
items.text:
The ./src bind mount in docker-compose.yml stays as it is — it now carries every project directory. Only the import root changes, from the mount point itself to this project's package directory:

      PYTHONPATH: /app/src/<package>/src

That is the point of the move: /app/src stops being a sys.path entry, so a checkout sitting next to your project can no longer contribute stray portions to a namespace package that shares its name.

Restart the backend to pick it up (the --reload=config flag covers config edits, not the compose file):

docker compose up -d backend
path: Move to the src/ project layout

items.title: 4. Add the src/ ignore rule
items.text:
Replace any per-checkout ignore lines with the rule they were standing in for, in the stack's .gitignore:

# Every entry under src/ is a project directory. This project's own
# package is tracked; anything else cloned there belongs to its own repo.
/src/*
!/src/<package>/

Add .venv/ too if it is not already there — each project directory gets its own.
path: Move to the src/ project layout

items.title: 5. Verify
items.text:
The library, from its own project directory:

cd src/<package>
uv sync
uv run pytest

The stack root, which is the half the migration is easiest to get wrong — both commands fail loudly if [project] or [dependency-groups] went missing in step 2:

cd <stack>
uv sync                 # must not warn "No requires-python value found"
uv run zensical build   # must not fail with "Failed to spawn: zensical"

Then open the custom room and ask it to greet someone: that exercises the dotted <package>.tools.greeting name through the new PYTHONPATH.
path: Move to the src/ project layout

items.title: Once converted
items.text: See Custom Python package for what to do when you clone another repo into src/, and compare the result against a reference stack (see the tip at the top of Upgrading an existing stack) for more than a smoke test.
path: Move to the src/ project layout

items.title: OIDC providers and stack-init
items.text:
Part of Upgrading an existing stack.

Walk this rung with the v0.21b1 skill release — its generator produces the rung's end state. The stack being upgraded names the release that generated it in its own [tool.soliplex-template] manifest — use that one when climbing from an older shape.

uv run <skill>/scripts/skill_versions.py upgrade v0.21b1

This rung changes no releases: soliplex, haiku.rag-slim and the web client stay where rung 6 left them. It changes how the stack decides whether to require sign-in, and adds a setup step that runs before up. What changes:

  • the backend never runs with --no-auth-mode: with no auth_systems in backend/environment/oidc/config.yaml it runs without authentication anyway, and the first provider turns authentication on
  • the placeholder keycloak provider and the keycloak/ directory go away; the skill's scripts/oidc_providers.py adds and removes real providers
  • nginx includes fragments from nginx/conf.d/, one of which names the provider the /ingester/ gate signs in with
  • the /ingester/ gate is in every stack, not only in stacks with a provider
  • a stack-init service brings the Soliplex databases to their current schema and runs the setup steps in stack-init/init.d/: one makes Soliplex's no-auth user an admin while the stack has no provider, which --no-auth-mode used to do implicitly; another adds the admin_users entry that admits the room provisioner

Where a step differs, it says which kind of stack it means:

  • a stack without a provider runs the backend with --no-auth-mode, and its oidc/config.yaml holds only the placeholder keycloak entry
  • a stack with a provider runs the backend without --no-auth-mode, and its oidc/config.yaml holds the provider(s) it signs in with

Skip the steps that do not apply. Each names what the current template has; compare against a stack the rung's release generates.

  1. Stop the stack with docker compose down, and back up the Postgres databases (see Before you start).

  2. Add the nginx fragment directory. Copy nginx/conf.d/README.md from the reference stack, so the directory exists in git. Then, in docker-compose.yml, mount it into the nginx service, after the mime.types bind:

          # Stack fragments (see nginx/conf.d/README.md): nginx reads them at
      # start, so restart nginx after adding or removing one.
      - type: bind
        source: ./nginx/conf.d
        target: /etc/nginx/conf.d
        read_only: true

  3. Include the fragments in both nginx servers. In nginx/nginx.conf, after the proxy_cookie_path / /; line in each server block (the HTTP one on 9000 and the HTTPS one on 9443):

            # Stack fragments: every '*.conf' under the stack's 'nginx/conf.d/'
        # (mounted read-only at /etc/nginx/conf.d/), included by both
        # servers. Skill scripts add and remove them, e.g. a route for an
        # added service. The variable below names the provider the
        # '/ingester/' gate signs in with: none until 'oidc_providers.py'
        # adds one and writes it into 'conf.d/signin-provider.conf'.
        set $soliplex_signin_provider "";
        include /etc/nginx/conf.d/*.conf;

  4. Gate /ingester/ in every stack.

    Compare nginx/nginx.conf with the reference stack's; the gate's parts are:

    • the map $http_sec_fetch_mode $soliplex_navigate block, before the first server
    • in each server, the location @ingester_signin and location = /_authz_check blocks
    • in each server's location /ingester/, the auth_request, auth_request_set and error_page 401 = @ingester_signin lines, and the X-Soliplex-User header

    In a stack without a provider, add them all, as the reference has them. In a stack with a provider, they are already there: change each @ingester_signin to the reference's, which redirects to the provider $soliplex_signin_provider names (not a fixed id such as keycloak) and answers signin_unavailable when none is set.

  5. Stop passing --no-auth-mode. In docker-compose.yml, delete the --no-auth-mode line from the backend service's command (in a stack without a provider; a stack with one has no such line), and replace the # Temporary: run with '--no-auth-mode' comment above it with the reference's.

  6. In a stack without a provider, remove the placeholder provider. Run the skill's oidc_providers.py from the stack directory; it leaves auth_systems: [] in backend/environment/oidc/config.yaml:

    uv run <skill>/scripts/oidc_providers.py remove keycloak

    Delete the keycloak/ directory too.

  7. In a stack with a provider, name the one /ingester/ signs in with: the id its old @ingester_signin redirected to. Run the skill's oidc_providers.py from the stack directory; it writes nginx/conf.d/signin-provider.conf:

    uv run <skill>/scripts/oidc_providers.py signin <id>

    Delete the keycloak/ directory if the stack has one.

  8. Add the stack-init service. Copy the stack-init/ directory from the reference stack. In docker-compose.yml, add the service after soliplex-provisioner; it reuses soliplex-dev's build, secrets and environment through their YAML anchors:

      # Prepares the stack before it first serves anyone, and again after a part
  # is added: brings the Soliplex databases to their current schema, then
  # runs every step in 'stack-init/init.d/' (see stack-init/README.md).
  # Every step is safe to re-run. Run it before 'docker compose up':
  #
  #   docker compose run --rm --quiet-build stack-init
  #
  # The 'soliplex-dev' image, secrets and environment (YAML aliases), so the
  # steps reach the databases as the backend does.
  stack-init:

    profiles: ["init"]

    build: *soliplex_dev_build

    env_file: ".env"
    user: "${PUID:-1000}:${PGID:-1000}"

    command: ["sh", "/stack-init/run.sh"]

    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy

    secrets: *soliplex_dev_secrets

    environment: *backend_environment

    volumes:
      - ./backend/environment:/environment/
      - ./src:/app/src:ro
      - ./stack-init:/stack-init:ro

  9. Run stack-init, then start.

    docker compose run --rm --quiet-build stack-init
docker compose up -d

    In a stack without a provider, --no-auth-mode already made the no-auth user an admin, so stack-init reports that fact. In a stack with a provider, it does not add the no-auth user as an admin.

    In both, it admits the room provisioner, unless rung 6's step 12 already did: it reports either way.

  10. Check it.

    Then open /ingester/ through nginx. In a stack without a provider, the dashboard opens with no sign-in.

    In a stack with a provider, it redirects to that provider's sign-in, and admits an admin after it.

    Commit.

items.title: Provision rooms on request
items.text:
Part of Upgrading an existing stack.

Walk this rung with the v0.20 skill release — its generator produces the rung's end state. The stack being upgraded names the release that generated it in its own [tool.soliplex-template] manifest — use that one when climbing from an older shape.

uv run <skill>/scripts/skill_versions.py upgrade v0.20

This rung moves the stack to soliplex 0.89 and haiku.rag-slim 0.104.0, and adds the room provisioner. What changes:

  • the releases: soliplex 0.87.0 to the moving 0.89 image tag, and the ingester from haiku.rag-slim 0.101.0 to 0.104.0; neither brings a RAG store migration, and the backend migrates its own databases on startup
  • the web client: frontend 0.110 to 0.114
  • the image builds freeze the soliplex image's packages as version pins, so an extra package that depends on soliplex installs
  • room uploads move from backend/uploads/ to a top-level uploads/
  • the room provisioner: a soliplex-provisioner service, the provisioned rooms' clone under src/rooms-provisioned, their shared provisioned_rag agent, and their database fragments, which the ingester includes
  • healthchecks check starting services every 2 seconds
  • in stacks with Gitea, its settings for the concierge's tracking issues

Skip the steps that do not apply. Each names what the current template has; compare against a stack the rung's release generates.

  1. Stop the stack with docker compose down, and back up the Postgres databases and rag/db/ (see Before you start).

  2. Bump the releases.

    • the FROM line in backend/Dockerfile: soliplex-postgres:0.87.0 becomes soliplex-postgres:0.89 (and in tui/Dockerfile, if the stack ships the TUI, soliplex-tui:0.89)
    • the ingester image in docker-compose.yml (the &haiku_rag_image anchor): haiku.rag-slim:0.101.0 becomes haiku.rag-slim:0.104.0
    • the FROM line in nginx/Dockerfile: frontend-web:0.110 becomes frontend-web:0.114
    • the manifest in pyproject.toml: soliplex_image_tag = "0.89", soliplex_dev_constraint = ">= 0.89, < 0.90", haiku_rag_version = "0.104.0" and frontend_version = "0.114"
    • the soliplex requirement in the root and package pyproject.toml files: >= 0.89, < 0.90; then run uv lock in each project

  3. Freeze the image's packages as version pins. In backend/Dockerfile, and twice in soliplex-dev/Dockerfile, the constraints step changes from

          uv pip freeze --python /app/.venv/bin/python \

    to

          uv pip list --format freeze --python /app/.venv/bin/python \

  4. Move room uploads to the top level.

    mv backend/uploads uploads

    Then, in docker-compose.yml:

    • in the backend service, the uploads bind's source: "backend/uploads" becomes source: "uploads"
    • in the soliplex-dev service, ./backend/uploads:/uploads/ becomes ./uploads:/uploads/

    And in .gitignore, the four backend/uploads/... lines become:

    uploads/rooms/*
uploads/threads/*
!uploads/rooms/.gitkeep
!uploads/threads/.gitkeep

  5. Update backend/environment/installation.yaml.

    • The URL_SAFE_TOKEN_SECRET secret reads the stack's url_safe_token_secret Docker secret first, so the backend and the provisioner sign and verify service tokens with one key. Add this source above its env_var source:

            - kind: "file_path"
        file_path: /run/secrets/url_safe_token_secret

    • Add the provisioned rooms' agent to agent_configs, before the title entry (with the stack's own chat model):

        - id: "provisioned_rag"
    model_name: "gpt-oss:latest"
    system_prompt: |
      You are a helpful agent.

      Answer from this room's knowledge base: use the 'rag' skill to ground
      every answer, and cite the documents you used. If the knowledge base
      does not contain the answer, say so plainly.

    • Add the provisioned rooms' clone to room_paths:

      room_paths:
  - "./rooms"
  - "/app/src/rooms-provisioned"

  6. Let the ingester include the provisioned rooms' fragments. In haiku.rag/haiku.rag.yaml, add, after the ingester: section:

    lancedb:
  databases:
    haiku.rag: /data/haiku.rag.lancedb

databases_include: rooms-provisioned/databases.d

    If the file has a lancedb.databases map already (see Ingesting multiple databases), keep it, and make sure it lists every database in ingester.databases, haiku.rag included: haiku.rag requires that once the fragments place theirs.

  7. Give soliplex-dev the provisioner. In soliplex-dev/Dockerfile, after FROM backend:

    ARG SOLIPLEX_TEMPLATE="soliplex-template[provisioner]>=0.20"

    and, after USER root:

    RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN --mount=from=uv,source=/uv,target=/usr/local/bin/uv \
    --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    uv pip list --format freeze --python /app/.venv/bin/python \
      > /tmp/base-constraints.txt && \
    uv pip install --python /app/.venv/bin/python \
      --constraints /tmp/base-constraints.txt \
      "$SOLIPLEX_TEMPLATE"

  8. Wire the provisioner into docker-compose.yml.

    • In the soliplex-dev service, name its build, secrets and volumes with anchors, so the new service can share them; add the ingester_bearer secret; and mount the ingester's config read-only:

          build: &soliplex_dev_build
      context: soliplex-dev
      additional_contexts:
        backend: "service:backend"

    secrets: &soliplex_dev_secrets
      - agui_db_password
      - authz_db_password
      - url_safe_token_secret
      # The room provisioner's credential for the ingester's '/reload'.
      - ingester_bearer

    volumes: &soliplex_dev_volumes
      - ./backend/environment:/environment/
      - ./backend/sandbox/workdirs:/sandbox/workdirs
      - ./uploads:/uploads/
      - ./rag/db:/db
      # src/ read-WRITE; the backend mounts the same tree read-only.
      - ./src:/app/src
      # The ingester's config: the room provisioner checks that it
      # includes the provisioned rooms' database fragments.
      - ./haiku.rag/haiku.rag.yaml:/app/haiku.rag.yaml:ro

    • Add the soliplex-provisioner service, after soliplex-dev:

        soliplex-provisioner:

    build: *soliplex_dev_build

    env_file: ".env"
    user: "${PUID:-1000}:${PGID:-1000}"

    working_dir: /app/src

    command:
      - /app/.venv/bin/uvicorn
      - --factory
      - soliplex_template.provision_service:create_app
      - --host=0.0.0.0
      - --port=8090

    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy

    healthcheck:
      test:
        - "CMD"
        - "python"
        - "-c"
        - "import urllib.request,sys; sys.exit(0 if urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8090/ok', timeout=5).status == 200 else 1)"
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 4
      start_period: 60s
      start_interval: 2s

    restart: unless-stopped

    secrets: *soliplex_dev_secrets

    environment: *backend_environment

    volumes: *soliplex_dev_volumes

    • In the haiku-ingester service's volumes (the &haiku_rag_volumes anchor, which the one-shot haiku-rag service shares), add the provisioned rooms' clone and the room uploads:

            # The provisioned-rooms clone: its 'databases.d' holds each
      # provisioned room's database fragment, which haiku.rag.yaml
      # includes.
      - ./src/rooms-provisioned:/app/rooms-provisioned:ro
      # Room uploads, the corpus of each room's own database.
      - ./uploads/rooms:/uploads/rooms:ro

    • Check starting services often: add to the backend healthcheck

            start_period: 120s
      start_interval: 2s

      and to the postgres healthcheck

            start_period: 30s
      start_interval: 2s

    • In stacks with Gitea, add to the gitea service's environment (after GITEA__server__ROOT_URL):

            GITEA__server__PUBLIC_URL_DETECTION: "legacy"
      GITEA__attachment__ALLOWED_TYPES: ".avif,.cpuprofile,.csv,.dmp,.docx,.fodg,.fodp,.fods,.fodt,.gif,.gz,.jpeg,.jpg,.json,.jsonc,.log,.md,.mov,.mp4,.odf,.odg,.odp,.ods,.odt,.patch,.pdf,.png,.pptx,.svg,.tgz,.txt,.webm,.webp,.xls,.xlsx,.yaml,.yml,.zip"

      Gitea then builds its links from ROOT_URL whichever host a request came through, and accepts the concierge's user-profile.yaml attachments.

  9. Create the provisioned rooms' clone directory, so Docker does not create the ingester's bind-mount source owned by root:

    mkdir -p src/rooms-provisioned

    The stack's .gitignore already ignores everything under src/ but its own project; the provisioner makes the directory a git repository of its own.

  10. Rebuild and start.

    docker compose build --pull backend soliplex-dev soliplex-provisioner nginx
docker compose up -d

    (Add tui to the build in stacks that ship it.) The soliplex-dev and soliplex-provisioner builds install soliplex-template[provisioner] 0.20 from PyPI.

    If the web client then stops at "probing providers", it is holding credentials stored by the old client: clear the browser's site data for the stack's address, and reload.

  11. In stacks with Gitea, provision its rooms repository. Run the stack's Gitea setup again: it is idempotent, and it now also creates the private soliplex-admin/rooms-provisioned repository the provisioner pushes to, and the tracking repository's provision-status labels. It rotates the service account's token, so recreate the services that read .env afterwards:

    uv run scripts/init_gitea.py
docker compose up -d backend soliplex-provisioner

  12. Admit the provisioner, in auth-mode stacks. The provisioner calls the backend with service tokens whose subject is soliplex-provisioner; admit them as an admin once (see Room provisioning):

    docker compose run --rm --quiet-build soliplex-dev \
    /app/.venv/bin/soliplex-cli admin-users add /environment \
    --json-path '$[?$.sub == "soliplex-provisioner"]'

    Until this entry exists, soliplex-provisioner reports unhealthy: its /ok answers 503, naming the problem, and its log names the admin_users entry it needs. It rechecks its access every 15 seconds, so it turns healthy without a restart.

    To let users other than admins request rooms through the provisioner service, write a policy for the reserved room id __provision__ (see The provisioner service).

  13. Check it. Then provision a test room, and check that it is live:

    uv run <skill>/scripts/provision_room.py --project-dir . \
    --username alice --name "Upgrade check"

    Commit.

items.title: The provisioner on soliplex-concierge
items.text:
Part of Upgrading an existing stack.

Walk this rung with the v0.21 skill release — its generator produces the rung's end state. The stack being upgraded names the release that generated it in its own [tool.soliplex-template] manifest — use that one when climbing from an older shape.

uv run <skill>/scripts/skill_versions.py upgrade v0.21

This rung changes no releases: soliplex, haiku.rag-slim and the web client stay where rung 7 left them. It moves the room provisioner onto soliplex-concierge's provisioner framework, which soliplex-template 0.21 depends on (soliplex-concierge[provisioner] >= 0.14). What changes:

  • the soliplex-provisioner service runs a new factory, soliplex_template.provisioner.wiring:create_app
  • stack-init's provisioner step imports from the new soliplex_template.provisioner package
  • the backend's environment, which soliplex-dev, soliplex-provisioner and stack-init share, sets SOLIPLEX_INSTALLATION_PATH, so soliplex-cli commands no longer need the installation's path
  • each room provisioned from now on records its request and its policy in the provisioned-rooms clone (provision.yaml, authz.yaml), and soliplex-provision-room --reconcile replays them (see Room provisioning)
  • in a stack with the concierge, reinstallint the about room enables the new provisioning features (see Rooms for someone else)

The old factory (soliplex_template.provision_service:create_app) and stack-init's old import still work in soliplex-template 0.21, so a stack that skips steps 3 and 4 keeps running. They are deprecated, and go in a later release.

Where a step differs, it says which kind of stack it means:

  • a stack with the concierge has a soliplex-concierge line in backend/requirements.txt, and an about-<project> room
  • a stack without the concierge has neither

Skip the steps that do not apply. Each names what the current template has; compare against a stack the rung's release generates.

  1. Stop the stack with docker compose down. This rung changes no database, so no backup is needed beyond your usual one.

  2. In a stack with the concierge, raise its pin to 0.14. In backend/requirements.txt, change the soliplex-concierge line's version to 0.14 (for example soliplex-concierge[truststore]==0.14). soliplex-dev installs soliplex-template 0.21 with the backend image's versions as constraints, so an older concierge pin makes its build fail.

  3. Run the new provisioner factory. In docker-compose.yml, in the soliplex-provisioner service's command:

          - soliplex_template.provisioner.wiring:create_app

    replacing soliplex_template.provision_service:create_app.

  4. Update stack-init's provisioner step. In stack-init/init.d/20-provisioner-admin.py, replace from soliplex_template import provision with:

    from soliplex_template.provisioner import adapters

    and provision.DEFAULT_SERVICE_SUBJECT with adapters.DEFAULT_SERVICE_SUBJECT.

  5. Set the installation path. In docker-compose.yml, add to the backend service's environment (the &backend_environment block), after PYTHONPATH:

          # 'soliplex-cli' commands work w/o explicit environment argument
      SOLIPLEX_INSTALLATION_PATH: /environment

  6. Install soliplex-template 0.21 in soliplex-dev. In soliplex-dev/Dockerfile, change the SOLIPLEX_TEMPLATE default:

    ARG SOLIPLEX_TEMPLATE="soliplex-template[provisioner]>=0.21"

  7. Rebuild, run stack-init, then start. The backend image rebuilds in a stack with the concierge, for its new pin; soliplex-dev and soliplex-provisioner rebuild in every stack:

    docker compose build backend soliplex-dev soliplex-provisioner
docker compose run --rm --quiet-build stack-init
docker compose up -d

  8. In a stack with the concierge, reinstall the about room with the soliplex-concierge-installer skill from soliplex-concierge's v0.14 release (installer 0.7.0 or later), passing --force and the Gitea owner and repository you installed it with. Its prompt now lets an admin request a room for someone else. --force replaces the room's files: compare git diff before you commit, and carry over any edits of your own. The reinstalled room_config.yaml starts with an # Installed by soliplex-concierge-installer <version> line.

  9. Reconcile, to see where the clone stands. Rooms provisioned before this rung have no authz.yaml; reconcile names them and leaves their policies alone:

    docker compose run --rm --quiet-build soliplex-dev \
    /app/.venv/bin/soliplex-provision-room --reconcile

  10. Check it.

    Then check that the provisioner service answers (GET /ok through the compose network, or docker compose ps soliplex-provisioner reporting it healthy).

    Commit.

items.title: Room id forms and tracker labels
items.text:
Part of Upgrading an existing stack.

Walk this rung with the v0.22 skill release — its generator produces the rung's end state. The stack being upgraded names the release that generated it in its own [tool.soliplex-template] manifest — use that one when climbing from an older shape.

uv run <skill>/scripts/skill_versions.py upgrade v0.22

This rung changes no releases: soliplex, haiku.rag-slim and the web client stay where rung 8 left them. It makes the room id's form configurable, tags the tracking issues with their provision status, and soliplex-template 0.22 depends on soliplex-concierge[provisioner] >= 0.15 for. What changes:

  • the room id's form is a setting (PROVISIONER_ROOM_ID_SEPARATOR; default --, the concierge's; : keeps the foremen:quarry-notes form rooms provisioned before rung 8 carry), as is the owner part's case (PROVISIONER_LOWERCASE_OWNER, default true)
  • soliplex-provision-room --reconcile honors the configured form: before, it read the clone against -- whatever it held
